title.zh: 卷356 列傳一百四十三 洪亮吉 管世铭 谷际岐 李仲昭 石承藻
title.en: Volume 356 Biographies 143: Hong Liangji, Guan Shiming, Gu Jiqi, Li Zhongzhao, Shi Chengzao
title.raw: 卷356 列傳一百四十三 洪亮吉 管世铭 谷际岐 李仲昭 石承藻

sentences.zh: 列傳一百四十三

translations.literal: Biographies, Number 143
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 143

sentences.zh: 洪亮吉管世銘谷際岐李仲昭石承藻

translations.literal: Hong Liangji, Guan Shiming, Gu Jiqi, Li Zhongzhao, and Shi Chengzao
translations.idiomatic: Hong Liangji, Guan Shiming, Gu Jiqi, Li Zhongzhao, and Shi Chengzao

sentences.zh: 洪亮吉，字稚存，江蘇陽湖人。

translations.literal: Hong Liangji, style name Zhicun, was a native of Yanghu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Liangji, whose style was Zhicun, came from Yanghu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，力學，孝事寡母。

translations.literal: He lost his father young and was poor, but studied diligently and served his widowed mother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early and raised in poverty, he threw himself into study and cared devotedly for his widowed mother.

sentences.zh: 初佐安徽學政硃筠校文，繼入​​陝西巡撫畢沅幕，為校刊古書。

translations.literal: At first he assisted Anhui Education Commissioner Zhu Yun in examining literary compositions; later he entered the staff of Shaanxi Governor Bi Yuan to collate and publish ancient books.
translations.idiomatic: He first helped Zhu Yun, the Anhui education commissioner, review examination essays, then joined Bi Yuan's staff in Shaanxi to edit and publish classical texts.

sentences.zh: 詞章考據，著於一時，尤精揅輿地。

translations.literal: His belles-lettres and evidential scholarship were renowned in his day, and he was especially skilled in researching geography and cosmography.
translations.idiomatic: His literary work and philological scholarship made him famous in his time, above all his expertise in historical geography.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十五年，成一甲第二名進士，授翰林院編修，年已四十有五。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year of the Qianlong reign he placed second in the first class of the jinshi examination and was appointed Hanlin Academician Compiler, by which time he was already forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In 1790 he took second place in the top tier of the palace examination and was made a Hanlin compiler at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 長身火色，性豪邁，喜論當世事。

translations.literal: Tall in stature and ruddy in complexion, he was bold in temperament and fond of discussing affairs of the day.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and ruddy-faced, he had a bold temperament and loved to debate current affairs.

sentences.zh: 未散館，分校順天鄉試。

translations.literal: Before completing his probation at the Hanlin Academy, he was assigned to grade the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Before finishing his Hanlin probation, he was put on the board that graded the Shuntian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 督貴州學政，以古學教士，地僻無書籍，購經、史、通典、文選置各府書院，黔士始治經史。

translations.literal: As Guizhou Education Commissioner he taught scholars the classical learning; the region was remote and lacked books, so he purchased the Classics, histories, the Tongdian, and the Wenxuan for the academies in each prefecture, and only then did Guizhou scholars begin to study the Classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: As Guizhou education commissioner he taught the classics. The province was remote and bookless, so he bought standard works—the Classics, histories, the Tongdian, and the Wenxuan—for every prefectural academy, and Guizhou scholars at last began serious study of the canon.

sentences.zh: 為詩古文有法。

translations.literal: His poetry and ancient-style prose followed proper methods.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were composed with real craft.

sentences.zh: 任滿還京，入直上書房，授皇曾孫奕純讀。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to the capital, entered the Imperial Study on direct appointment, and instructed the emperor's great-grandson Yi Chun in reading.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to Beijing, entered the Imperial Study, and tutored the emperor's great-grandson Yi Chun.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，大考翰詹，試徵邪教疏，亮吉力陳內外弊政數千言，為時所忌。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Jiaqing reign, at the great examination of Hanlin and Imperial Academy members, the topic was a memorial on suppressing heterodox sects; Liangji forcefully set forth several thousand characters on abuses at court and in the provinces, and was resented by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1798, at the triennial Hanlin examination, candidates were asked to draft a memorial on sectarian rebellion. Liangji poured thousands of words into a blunt catalogue of abuses at court and in the provinces, and made powerful enemies.

sentences.zh: 以弟喪陳情歸。

translations.literal: He submitted a petition on account of his younger brother's death and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded a brother's death and went home.

sentences.zh: 四年，高宗崩，仁宗始親政。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Gaozong Emperor died and the Renzong Emperor began to rule in person.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799 the Qianlong emperor died and the Jiaqing emperor took the reins himself.

sentences.zh: 大學士硃珪書起之，供職，與修高宗實錄，第一次稿本成，意有不樂。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhu Gui summoned him back by letter; he took office and helped compile the Veritable Records of Gaozong. When the first draft was finished he was displeased in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhu Gui recalled him by letter. He resumed office and worked on the Qianlong Veritable Records, but when the first draft was done he was deeply dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 將告歸，上書軍機王大臣言事，略曰：「今天子求治之心急矣，天下望治之心孔迫矣，而機局未轉者，推原其故，蓋有數端。

translations.literal: About to request leave and return home, he submitted a letter to the Grand Council minister Wang stating his views, in summary as follows: "Today the Son of Heaven's desire for good government is urgent, and the empire's longing for good government is exceedingly pressing, yet the machinery of state has not turned—tracing the causes, there are several.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of resigning he sent a long letter to Grand Councilor Wang. It began: "The emperor's hunger for reform is keen and the empire's longing for order still keener, yet the machinery of government has barely moved. The reasons, I believe, are several.

sentences.zh: 亮吉以為勵精圖治，當一法祖宗初政之勤，而尚未盡法也。

translations.literal: Liangji held that in striving for diligent rule one ought wholly to follow the diligence of the founding policies of the ancestors, yet this had not been fully followed.
translations.idiomatic: Liangji argued that reviving government should mean matching the diligence of the dynasty's early reigns—and that standard had not yet been met.

sentences.zh: 用人行政，當一改權臣當國之時，而尚未盡改也。

translations.literal: In employing men and administering affairs one ought to change completely the conditions of the time when powerful ministers held the state, yet this had not been fully changed.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments and policy ought to break decisively with the era of domineering ministers—and that break was still incomplete.

sentences.zh: 風俗則日趨卑下，賞罰則仍不嚴明，言路則似通而未通，吏治則欲肅而未肅。

translations.literal: Customs daily sank lower; rewards and punishments were still not strict and clear; the avenue of remonstrance seemed open yet was not truly open; and official administration wished to be rectified yet was not truly rectified.
translations.idiomatic: Morals were sinking day by day; rewards and punishments remained lax; the path of candid counsel looked open but was not; and the bureaucracy was meant to be tightened but was not.

sentences.zh: 何以言勵精圖治尚未盡法也？

translations.literal: Why say that striving for diligent rule has not yet been fully followed?
translations.idiomatic: Why had revival of government not yet been achieved?

sentences.zh: 自三四月以來，視朝稍晏，竊恐退朝之後，俳優近習之人，熒惑聖聽者不少。

translations.literal: Since the third and fourth months audiences have been held somewhat late; I fear that after leaving court, actors and intimate attendants who beguile the imperial ear are not few.
translations.idiomatic: Since spring, audiences had been held later and later. I feared that after court, actors and favored attendants were misleading the emperor in no small number.

sentences.zh: 此親臣大臣啟沃君心者之過也。

translations.literal: This is the fault of intimate ministers and great officials who ought to nourish the ruler's mind.
translations.idiomatic: That was the fault of the intimate ministers who were supposed to guide the ruler's mind.

sentences.zh: 蓋犯顏極諫，雖非親臣大臣之事，然不可使國家無嚴憚之人。

translations.literal: For although risking one's life in blunt remonstrance is not the special duty of intimate ministers, the state must not be without men whom others deeply fear.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt remonstrance at the risk of one's life was not their special duty, yet the state could not afford to lack men whom others deeply feared.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初年，純皇帝宵旰不遑，勤求至治，其時如鄂文端、硃文端、張文和、孫文定等，皆侃侃以老成師傅自居。

translations.literal: In the early Qianlong years the Chun Emperor toiled from dawn till midnight without rest, diligently seeking perfect rule; at that time men such as E Wen-duan, Zhu Wen-duan, Zhang Wen-he, and Sun Wen-ding all spoke forthrightly and took themselves to be seasoned tutors.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianlong years the emperor labored from dawn to midnight in pursuit of perfect government. Men such as E Zhun, Zhu Shi, Zhang Tingyu, and Sun Jiagan spoke plainly and styled themselves seasoned mentors of the throne.

sentences.zh: 亮吉恭修實錄，見一日中硃筆細書，折成方寸，或詢張、鄂，或詢孫、硃，曰某人賢否，某事當否，日或十馀次。

translations.literal: Liangji, in reverently compiling the Veritable Records, saw that in a single day the vermilion brush would write fine characters folded to an inch square, now asking Zhang or E, now asking Sun or Zhu, whether a certain man was worthy or unworthy, whether a certain matter ought to be done or not—sometimes more than ten times a day.
translations.idiomatic: While helping compile the Veritable Records, Liangji saw how in a single day the emperor's vermilion brush would jot tiny folded notes—now asking Zhang or E, now Sun or Zhu, whether so-and-so was fit for office or whether such-and-such ought to be done—sometimes a dozen times in one day.

sentences.zh: 諸臣亦皆隨時隨事奏片，質語直陳，是上下無隱情。

translations.literal: The various ministers also submitted memorial slips on every occasion and matter, speaking plainly in direct language, so that above and below there were no hidden facts.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers likewise filed timely memorial slips in plain, direct language, so that nothing was hidden between throne and officials.

sentences.zh: 純皇帝固聖不可及，而亦眾正盈朝，前後左右皆嚴憚之人故也。

translations.literal: The Chun Emperor was indeed sage beyond reach, but it was also because upright men filled the court and those before, behind, left, and right were all men deeply feared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's sagacity was beyond compare, but it also helped that upright men filled the court and that everyone around him was someone to be feared.

sentences.zh: 今一則處事太緩，自乾隆五十五年以後，權私蒙蔽，事事不得其平者，不知凡幾矣。

translations.literal: Now, first, affairs are handled too slowly; since the fifty-fifth year of Qianlong, private power has veiled the truth, and cases in which things were not settled fairly—who knows how many?
translations.idiomatic: Today, first, business moved too slowly. Since 1790 private interests had clouded judgment, and wrongs left unsettled were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 千百中無有一二能上達者，即能上達，未必即能見之施行也。

translations.literal: Of a thousand or hundred cases scarcely one or two could reach the throne; even if they did reach it, they might not necessarily be seen and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Of hundreds of grievances scarcely one or two reached the throne, and even then they might never be acted on.

sentences.zh: 如江南洋盜一案，參將楊天相有功駢戮，洋盜某漏網安居，皆由署總督蘇凌阿昏憒糊塗，貪贓玩法，舉世知其冤，而洋盜公然上岸無所顧忌，皆此一事釀成。

translations.literal: Take the Jiangnan pirate case: Battalion Commander Yang Tianxiang, who had merit, was executed together with others, while a certain pirate escaped the net and lived at ease—all because Acting Governor Su Ling'a was muddled and stupid, greedy for bribes and contemptuous of law. The whole world knew his injustice, yet pirates openly came ashore without fear; all this was brewed by that one affair.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Jiangnan pirate case: Battalion Commander Yang Tianxiang, a man with real merit, was executed in a mass killing while a pirate went free—all because Acting Governor Su Ling'a was muddled, greedy, and lawless. Everyone knew Yang had been wronged, yet pirates now landed openly without fear. One botched case had taught them they could.

sentences.zh: 況蘇凌阿權相私人，朝廷必無所顧惜，而至今尚擁巨貲，厚自頤養。

translations.literal: Moreover Su Ling'a was a private man of the powerful minister; the court ought certainly not to spare him, yet to this day he still holds great wealth and nourishes himself lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, Su Ling'a was a creature of the late power-holder; the court owed him no tenderness, yet he still sat on a fortune and lived in comfort.

sentences.zh: 江南查辦此案，始則有心為承審官開釋，繼則並聞以不冤覆奏。

translations.literal: In Jiangnan's investigation of this case, at first there was intent to exonerate the presiding judge; later it was even heard that a memorial was submitted covering the matter as not unjust.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan inquiry first seemed bent on excusing the presiding judge; later word came that the court had been told there was no injustice at all.

sentences.zh: 夫以聖天子赫然獨斷，欲平反一事而尚如此，則此外沉冤何自而雪乎？

translations.literal: If with the sage Son of Heaven's august independent decision, wishing to reverse one case, it is still thus, then how can other submerged wrongs ever be cleared?
translations.idiomatic: If even when the sage emperor himself intervened to right one case the outcome was still such, how were all the other buried wrongs ever to be cleared?

sentences.zh: 一則集思廣益之法未備。

translations.literal: Second, the method of gathering many thoughts to broaden benefit is not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the methods for pooling counsel had not been put in place.

sentences.zh: 堯、舜之主，亦必詢四岳，詢群牧。

translations.literal: Even rulers like Yao and Shun must inquire of the Four Peaks and inquire of the various pastors.
translations.idiomatic: Even rulers as great as Yao and Shun questioned the Four Peaks and the regional lords.

sentences.zh: 蓋恐一人之聰明有限，必博收眾採，庶無失事。

translations.literal: For they feared that one man's intelligence is limited; one must broadly gather and widely collect, so that nothing is missed.
translations.idiomatic: One man's wit is limited; only by gathering many voices could mistakes be avoided.

sentences.zh: 請自今凡召見大小臣工，必詢問人材，詢問利弊。

translations.literal: I ask that from now on, whenever great and small officials are received in audience, the ruler must inquire about talent and inquire about advantages and disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whenever officials of any rank were received in audience, let the emperor ask about talent and about what policies helped or harmed the realm.

sentences.zh: 所言可採，則存檔冊以記之。

translations.literal: If what is said can be adopted, then store it in registers for record.
translations.idiomatic: Sound advice should be entered in the archives.

sentences.zh: 倘所舉非人，所言失實，則治其失言之罪。

translations.literal: If those recommended are unworthy or what is said is untrue, then punish the offense of erroneous speech.
translations.idiomatic: If a man recommended proved unfit or his report false, let him be punished for misleading the throne.

sentences.zh: 然寄耳目於左右近習，不可也；

translations.literal: Yet to entrust one's eyes and ears to intimate attendants at one's side—this cannot be done;
translations.idiomatic: Yet one must not rely on intimate attendants for one's eyes and ears;

sentences.zh: 詢人之功過於其黨類，亦不可也。

translations.literal: nor to inquire about a man's merits and faults from his faction—this also cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: nor ask a man's clique about his merits and faults.

sentences.zh: 蓋人材至今日，銷磨殆盡矣。

translations.literal: For talent by today has been worn down nearly to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Talent, by now, had been ground nearly away.

sentences.zh: 以模棱為曉事，以軟弱為良圖，以鑽營為取進之階，以苟且為服官之計。

translations.literal: They take equivocation for understanding affairs, weakness for a good plan, wire-pulling for the ladder of advancement, and temporizing for the strategy of holding office.
translations.idiomatic: Men took equivocation for wisdom, timidity for prudence, intrigue for the path to promotion, and muddling through for the art of office.

sentences.zh: 由此道者，無不各得其所欲而去，衣缽相承，牢結而不可解。

translations.literal: Those who follow this path all depart having gained what they desire; the robe and bowl are handed down in succession, bound fast and impossible to undo.
translations.idiomatic: All who lived by that code left with what they wanted; the habit passed from hand to hand like a master's robe and bowl, knotted tight beyond undoing.

sentences.zh: 夫此模棱、軟弱、鑽營、苟且之人，國家無事，以之備班列可也；

translations.literal: Such equivocating, weak, wire-pulling, temporizing men, when the state has no troubles, may serve to fill the ranks;
translations.idiomatic: In quiet times such equivocators, weaklings, schemers, and temporizers might suffice to fill the ranks;

sentences.zh: 適有緩急，而慾望其奮身為國，不顧利害，不計夷險，不瞻徇情面，不顧惜身家，不可得也。

translations.literal: but when urgency arises, to expect them to throw themselves forward for the state, heedless of advantage and harm, reckoning neither ease nor danger, neither looking to personal ties nor sparing their persons and families—this cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: but in crisis one could not expect them to throw themselves into the state's service heedless of gain or loss, ease or danger, favor or family.

sentences.zh: 至於利弊之不講，又非一日。

translations.literal: As for the failure to discuss advantages and disadvantages, this too is not a matter of a single day.
translations.idiomatic: The refusal to weigh policy's costs and benefits was nothing new either.

sentences.zh: 在內部院諸臣，事本不多，而常若猝猝不暇，汲​​汲顧影，皆云多一事不如少一事。

translations.literal: Among ministers within the boards and courts, their business is not much, yet they always seem hurried and without leisure, anxiously watching their shadows, all saying that one more matter is not as good as one less.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the capital boards, business was not heavy, yet ministers acted perpetually rushed and anxious, all chanting that one trouble spared was better than one taken on.

sentences.zh: 在外督撫諸臣，其賢者斤斤自守，不肖者亟亟營私。

translations.literal: Among governors and governors-general outside, the worthy guard every inch for themselves, while the unworthy hurry to pursue private gain.
translations.idiomatic: Among provincial governors, the worthy clung narrowly to their own integrity while the unworthy scrambled for private profit.

sentences.zh: 國計民生，非所計也，救目前而已；

translations.literal: National revenue and the people's livelihood are not what they calculate—only rescuing the present moment;
translations.idiomatic: National finances and people's livelihoods were not their concern—only the crisis of the moment;

sentences.zh: 官方吏治，非所急也，保本任而已。

translations.literal: official standards and administration of officials are not what they urgently pursue—only preserving their own tenure.
translations.idiomatic: official discipline was not urgent—only keeping their own posts.

sentences.zh: 慮久遠者，以為過憂；

translations.literal: Those who consider the long term are deemed to worry excessively;
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who looked ahead was called an alarmist;

sentences.zh: 事興革者，以為生事。

translations.literal: those who undertake innovation and reform are deemed to stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: anyone who pushed reform was called a troublemaker.

sentences.zh: 此又豈國家求治之本意乎？

translations.literal: Is this again the original intent of the state's pursuit of good government?
translations.idiomatic: Was that what the state meant by seeking good government?

sentences.zh: 二則進賢退不肖似尚游移。

translations.literal: Second, advancing the worthy and removing the unworthy still seems hesitant and wavering.
translations.idiomatic: Second, promoting the worthy and removing the unworthy still seemed hesitant and half-hearted.

sentences.zh: 夫邪教之起，由於激變。

translations.literal: The rise of heterodox sects stems from harsh provocation.
translations.idiomatic: Sectarian rebellion arose from official cruelty and provocation.

sentences.zh: 原任達州知州戴如煌，罪不容逭矣。

translations.literal: The former Dazhou Prefect Dai Ruhuang's crimes admit no escape.
translations.idiomatic: The former prefect of Dazhou, Dai Ruhuang, deserved no mercy.

sentences.zh: 幸有一眾口交譽之劉清，百姓服之，教匪亦服之。

translations.literal: Fortunately there is a Liu Qing whom all mouths praise together; the common people submit to him, and the sect rebels also submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately there was Liu Qing, praised on every side—trusted by the people and even by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 此時正當用明效大驗之人。

translations.literal: At this time one ought precisely to employ men of clear effect and great proof.
translations.idiomatic: This was the moment to use men whose merit had already been proved in plain sight.

sentences.zh: 聞劉清尚為州牧，僅從司道之後辦事，似不足盡其長矣。

translations.literal: I hear Liu Qing is still a prefect, merely handling affairs behind the provincial and circuit officials—this seems insufficient to exhaust his strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Qing was still only a prefect, working behind his superiors—hardly enough to use his full capacity.

sentences.zh: 亮吉以為川省多事，經略縱極嚴明，勦賊匪用之，撫難民用之，整飭官方辦理地方之事又用之，此不能分身者也。

translations.literal: Liangji holds that Sichuan has many troubles; however strict and clear the commissioner-general may be, he must use himself to suppress bandits, use himself to pacify suffering people, and use himself again to rectify officials and handle local affairs—this is what one man cannot divide.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan was in turmoil. However able the commissioner-general, he needed himself to fight rebels, pacify the people, and straighten out local government—one man could not do everything.

sentences.zh: 何如擇此方賢吏如劉清者，崇其官爵，假以事權，使之一意招徠撫綏，以分督撫之權，以蕆國家之事。

translations.literal: Why not select worthy local officials of this region such as Liu Qing, elevate their rank and titles, lend them administrative authority, and let them devote themselves to winning people over and pacifying them, thereby dividing the power of governors and completing the state's affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Why not pick proven local men like Liu Qing, raise their rank, give them real authority, and let them win people back while sharing the governors' burden and finishing the state's work?

sentences.zh: 有明中葉以來，鄖陽多事，則別設鄖陽巡撫；

translations.literal: Since the mid-Ming, when Yunyang had many troubles, a separate Yunyang governor-general was established;
translations.idiomatic: In mid-Ming times, when Yunyang was troubled, a separate Yunyang governor was appointed;

sentences.zh: 偏沅多事，則別設偏沅巡撫。

translations.literal: when Pian-Yuan had many troubles, a separate Pian-Yuan governor-general was established.
translations.idiomatic: when the Hunan frontier was troubled, a separate Pian-Yuan governor was appointed.

sentences.zh: 事竣則撤之，此不可拘拘於成例者也。

translations.literal: When affairs were concluded they were withdrawn—this is what cannot be bound rigidly by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis ended the post was abolished. One must not be slaves to precedent.

sentences.zh: 夫設官以待賢能，人果賢能，似不必過循資格。

translations.literal: Offices are established to await the worthy and able; if a man is truly worthy and able, it seems one need not overly follow seniority and qualification.
translations.idiomatic: Posts exist to employ talent; where talent is real, seniority need not rule.

sentences.zh: 如劉清者，進而尚未進也。

translations.literal: As for one like Liu Qing, he ought to advance yet has not yet advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Liu Qing ought to rise—and had not.

sentences.zh: 戴如煌雖以別案解任，然尚安處川中。

translations.literal: Although Dai Ruhuang was removed from office on another case, he still dwells at ease in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Ruhuang had been removed on another charge, yet still lived comfortably in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 聞教匪甘心欲食其肉，知其所在，即極力焚劫。

translations.literal: I hear the sect rebels are willing at heart to eat his flesh; knowing where he is, they immediately exert all force to burn and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were said to long to devour him alive; wherever he was found they burned and looted with all their might.

sentences.zh: 是以數月必移一處，教匪亦必隨而蹟之。

translations.literal: Therefore every few months he must move to another place, and the sect rebels also inevitably track his trail.
translations.idiomatic: So every few months he had to move, and the rebels tracked him wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 近在川東與一道員聯姻，恃以無恐。

translations.literal: Recently in eastern Sichuan he formed a marriage alliance with a circuit intendant and relies on this to feel no fear.
translations.idiomatic: Lately in eastern Sichuan he had married into a circuit intendant's family and felt secure.

sentences.zh: 是救一有罪之人，反殺千百無罪之人，其理尚可恕乎？

translations.literal: To save one guilty man while instead killing hundreds and thousands of innocent men—can this principle still be forgiven?
translations.idiomatic: To spare one guilty man while thousands of innocents died for it—could that be justified?

sentences.zh: 純皇帝大事之時，即明發諭旨數和珅之罪，並一一指其私人，天下快心。

translations.literal: At the time of the Chun Emperor's great mourning, he immediately issued open edicts enumerating Heshen's crimes and pointing out one by one his private men—the whole realm rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: At the Qianlong emperor's death the throne had openly listed Heshen's crimes and named his creatures one by one, to the nation's relief.

sentences.zh: 乃未幾而又起吳省蘭矣，召見之時，又聞其為吳省欽辨冤矣。

translations.literal: Yet before long Wu Shenglan rose again; at the time of his audience it was again heard that he was pleading innocence for Wu Shengqin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet soon Wu Shenglan was back in favor, and at his audience he was said to be pleading his brother Wu Shengqin's innocence.

sentences.zh: 夫二吳之為和珅私人，與之交通貨賄，人人所知。

translations.literal: That the two Wu were Heshen's private men and trafficked in bribes with him is known to everyone.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew the two Wu were Heshen's men and had traded in bribes with him.

sentences.zh: 故曹錫寶之糾和珅家人劉全也，以同鄉素好，先以摺稿示二吳，二吳即袖其走權門，藉為進身之地。

translations.literal: When Cao Xibao impeached Heshen's household servant Liu Quan, being fellow-townsmen on good terms he first showed the memorial draft to the two Wu; the two Wu immediately tucked it away and ran to the power-holders' gates, using it as a place to advance themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Xibao impeached Heshen's servant Liu Quan, he showed the draft first to the two Wu as fellow townsmen; they tucked it away and rushed to the power-holders, turning betrayal into advancement.

sentences.zh: 今二吳可雪，不幾與褒贈曹錫寶之明旨相戾乎？

translations.literal: If now the two Wu can be cleared, does this not nearly contradict the clear edict that honored and rewarded Cao Xibao?
translations.idiomatic: If the two Wu were now cleared, would that not flatly contradict the edict that had honored Cao Xibao?

sentences.zh: 夫吳省欽之傾險，秉文衡，尹京兆，無不聲名狼藉，則革職不足蔽辜矣。

translations.literal: As for Wu Shengqin's treacherous cunning, whether holding the literary balance, governing Jingzhao, in every case his reputation was in ruins—then dismissal from office is insufficient to cover his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shengqin's treachery had left his name in ruins whether as chief examiner or as Jingzhao intendant; dismissal alone could not answer for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 吳省蘭先為和珅教習師，後反稱和珅為老師，大考則第一矣，視學典試不絕矣，非和珅之力而誰力乎？

translations.literal: Wu Shenglan first was Heshen's tutoring master, then in turn called Heshen his teacher; in the great examination he took first place, and appointments as education commissioner and chief examiner never ceased—if not by Heshen's power, then by whose?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shenglan had once been Heshen's tutor, then called Heshen his teacher; he took first in the Hanlin examination and kept receiving education and examination posts—whose power was that if not Heshen's?

sentences.zh: 則降官亦不足蔽辜矣。

translations.literal: Then demotion in rank is also insufficient to cover his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Demotion in rank was likewise too light a penalty.

sentences.zh: 是退而尚未退也。

translations.literal: Thus they ought to be removed yet have not yet been removed.
translations.idiomatic: So the unworthy were meant to go—and had not truly gone.

sentences.zh: 何以言用人行政未盡改也？

translations.literal: Why say that employing men and administering affairs has not yet been fully changed?
translations.idiomatic: Why had appointments and policy not yet been fully reformed?

sentences.zh: 蓋其人雖已致法，而十馀年來，其更變祖宗成例，汲引一己私人，猶未嘗平心討論。

translations.literal: For although that man has already been brought to law, over more than ten years his alterations of the ancestors' established precedents and drawing in of his own private men have still never been calmly discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Though Heshen himself had been punished, more than ten years of his changes to ancestral precedent and packing of offices with his creatures had never been calmly reviewed.

sentences.zh: 內閣、六部各衙門，何為國家之成法，何為和珅所更張，誰為國家自用之人，誰為和珅所引進，以及隨同受賄舞弊之人，皇上縱極仁慈，縱慾寬脅從，又因人數甚廣，不能一切屏除。

translations.literal: In the Grand Secretariat, the Six Ministries, and each yamen—what was the state's established law, what was changed by Heshen, who were men the state employed for itself, who were introduced by Heshen, and those who together accepted bribes and committed malfeasance—the emperor, however extremely merciful, however wishing to pardon the coerced, and because the number of persons is very broad, cannot remove them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the Grand Secretariat, the Six Ministries, and every yamen—which rules were the state's and which Heshen's, who had been the court's own men and who Heshen's creatures, who had shared in bribery and fraud—the emperor might be merciful and wish to spare the coerced, and the numbers were too vast to purge everyone at once.

sentences.zh: 然竊以為實有真知灼見者，自不究其從前，亦當籍其姓名，於升遷調補之時，微示以善惡勸懲之法，使人人知聖天子雖不為已甚，而是非邪正之辨，未嘗不洞悉，未嘗不區別。

translations.literal: Yet I venture to hold that for those who truly have penetrating insight, even if one does not investigate their past, one should still register their names; at the time of promotion, transfer, and supplementation, subtly show the method of encouraging good and punishing evil, so that everyone knows that although the sage Son of Heaven does not go to excess, the distinction between right and wrong, orthodox and deviant, has never failed to be thoroughly understood and never failed to be differentiated.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for men of real insight, even without prosecuting the past, their names should be recorded; at every promotion or transfer let a quiet signal show reward and punishment, so all would know that though the emperor would not go to extremes, he still saw clearly who was upright and who was not.

sentences.zh: 如是而夙昔之為私人者，尚可革面革心而為國家之人。

translations.literal: Thus those who in former days were private men might still change face and change heart and become men of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Then even former creatures of the faction might turn anew and serve the state in earnest.

sentences.zh: 否則，朝廷常若今日清明可也，萬一他日復有效權臣所為者，而諸臣又群起而集其門矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, while the court may always be as clear as today, if someday there should again be one who imitates what the powerful minister did, the various officials will again rise as a group and gather at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the court might stay clear for a day, but if another power-holder rose tomorrow the officials would flock to his gate again.

sentences.zh: 何以言風俗日趨卑下也？

translations.literal: Why say that customs daily sink lower?
translations.idiomatic: Why did he say morals were sinking day by day?

sentences.zh: 士大夫漸不顧廉恥，百姓則不顧綱常。

translations.literal: The scholar-officials gradually cease to regard integrity and shame; the common people then cease to regard the moral order.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials no longer cared for integrity, and the people no longer cared for the moral order.

sentences.zh: 然此不當責之百姓，仍當責之士大夫也。

translations.literal: Yet this ought not to be charged to the common people; it should still be charged to the scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: But the blame lay not with the people—it lay with the scholar-official class.

sentences.zh: 以亮吉所見，十馀年來，有尚書、侍郎甘為宰相屈膝者矣；

translations.literal: In what Liangji has seen over more than ten years, there have been ministers and vice-ministers willing to bend the knee to the chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: In Liangji's own observation over more than ten years, ministers and vice-ministers had willingly knelt to the chief minister;

sentences.zh: 有大學士、七卿之長，且年長以倍，而求拜門生，求為私人者矣；

translations.literal: there have been grand secretaries and heads of the Seven Chief Ministries, though twice his senior in years, who sought to become his disciples and sought to become his private men;
translations.idiomatic: grand secretaries and heads of the chief ministries, though twice the minister's age, who sought to enroll as his disciples and become his creatures;

sentences.zh: 有交宰相之僮隸，並樂與抗禮者矣。

translations.literal: there have been those who associated with the chief minister's boy servants and were even pleased to exchange courtesies on equal terms.
translations.idiomatic: men who socialized with the minister's page boys and treated them as equals with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 太學三館，風氣之所由出也。

translations.literal: The Imperial University and the Three Academies are where the prevailing tone originates.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial University and the Three Academies were where public tone was formed.

sentences.zh: 今則有昏夜乞憐，以求署祭酒者矣；

translations.literal: Now there are those who beg piteously in the dark of night to obtain acting appointment as university chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Now men begged by night for acting appointment as university chancellor;

sentences.zh: 有人前長跪，以求講官者矣。

translations.literal: there are those who prostrate themselves in long kneeling before others to obtain lectureship posts.
translations.idiomatic: and prostrated themselves in public to win lectureship posts.

sentences.zh: 翰林大考，國家所據以升黜詞臣者也。

translations.literal: The Hanlin great examination is what the state relies on to promote and demote literary officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin great examination was how the state promoted and demoted its literary officers.

sentences.zh: 今則有先走軍機章京之門，求認師生，以探取御製詩韻者矣；

translations.literal: Now there are those who first run to the doors of Grand Council clerks, seek to be recognized as teacher and student, in order to probe and obtain the rhyme schemes of the emperor's composed poems;
translations.idiomatic: Now candidates ran first to Grand Council clerks, claimed them as teachers, and tried to learn the rhyme schemes of the emperor's examination poems in advance;

sentences.zh: 行賄於門闌侍衛，以求傳遞代倩，藏捲而去，制就而入者矣。

translations.literal: bribe the gate guards and attendants in order to have papers passed and answers written for them, hide the examination booklet and leave, then enter with the composition already finished.
translations.idiomatic: bribed gate guards to carry papers out and back, hid their booklets while answers were written for them, and re-entered with finished compositions.

sentences.zh: 及人人各得所欲，則居然自以為得計。

translations.literal: When each person each obtains what he desires, then calmly he considers himself to have hit upon a successful plan.
translations.idiomatic: Once everyone got what he wanted, he calmly assumed he had found a winning scheme.

sentences.zh: 夫大考如此，何以責鄉會試之懷挾替代？

translations.literal: If the great examination is thus, how can one blame the provincial and metropolitan examinations for carrying forbidden materials and substitution?
translations.idiomatic: If the Hanlin great examination was like this, how could one condemn the provincial and metropolitan exams for smuggling in crib sheets and stand-ins?

sentences.zh: 士大夫之行如此，何以責小民之誇詐夤緣？

translations.literal: If the conduct of scholar-officials is thus, how can one blame common people for boastful fraud and crony climbing?
translations.idiomatic: If the conduct of the literati was like this, how could one blame commoners for boastful fraud and backdoor dealings?

sentences.zh: 輦轂之下如此，何以責四海九州之營私舞弊？

translations.literal: If under the imperial capital it is thus, how can one blame the four seas and nine provinces for pursuing private gain and fraudulent practice?
translations.idiomatic: If things were like this at the capital itself, how could one blame the provinces for private profiteering and fraud?

sentences.zh: 純皇帝因內閣學士許玉猷為同姓石工護喪，諭廷臣曰：'諸臣縱不自愛，如國體何？

translations.literal: The Pure Emperor, because Grand Secretariat academician Xu Yuyou had a stonemason of the same surname attend his mourning, instructed the court ministers, saying: 'Even if you ministers do not care for yourselves, what of the national dignity?'
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor, learning that Grand Secretariat academician Xu Yuyou had a stonemason of the same surname attend his mourning, told the court: 'Even if you ministers care nothing for yourselves, what of the dignity of the state?'

sentences.zh: '是知國體之尊，在諸臣各知廉恥。

translations.literal: From this one knows that the honor of the national dignity lies in each minister knowing shame and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one sees that the honor of the state rests on every minister knowing shame and integrity.

sentences.zh: 夫下之化上，猶影響也。

translations.literal: The transformation of the lower by the upper is like shadow and echo.
translations.idiomatic: The lower orders take their cue from above as surely as a body casts a shadow.

sentences.zh: 士氣必待在上者振作之，風節必待在上者獎成之。

translations.literal: Scholarly morale must wait for those above to rouse it; moral integrity must wait for those above to reward and complete it.
translations.idiomatic: Scholarly morale must be revived from above; moral integrity must be fostered and rewarded from above.

sentences.zh: 舉一廉樸之吏，則貪欺者庶可自愧矣；

translations.literal: To recommend one honest and plain official, then the greedy and deceitful might feel shame;
translations.idiomatic: Promote one honest, unassuming official, and the greedy and deceitful might feel ashamed;

sentences.zh: 進一恬退之流，則奔競者庶可稍改矣；

translations.literal: To advance one retiring and unambitious sort, then the scrambling competitors might slightly reform;
translations.idiomatic: advance one who is content to stand aside, and the office-seekers might mend their ways a little;

sentences.zh: 拔一特立獨行、敦品勵節之士，則如脂如韋、依附朋比之風或可漸革矣。

translations.literal: To elevate one who stands alone in conduct and cultivates character and integrity, then the tendency to be slick as grease or pliant as leather and cling to faction might gradually be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: raise up a man of independent conduct who cultivates character and integrity, and the fashion for slick flattery and cliquish dependence might slowly change.

sentences.zh: 而亮吉更有所慮者，前之所言，皆士大夫之不務名節者耳。

translations.literal: But Liangji has a further worry: what was said before concerns only scholar-officials who do not pursue reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liangji has a further worry: what I have described so far concerns only those literati who neglect reputation and integrity.

sentences.zh: 幸有矯矯自好者，類皆惑於因果，遁入虛無，以蔬食為家規，以談禪為國政。

translations.literal: Fortunately there are those who stand aloof and prize their own standards, but most are confused by karma and cause-effect, flee into emptiness, take vegetable diet as family rule, and take Chan talk as state policy.
translations.idiomatic: There are also men of proud independence—but most of them are lost in doctrines of karma, retreat into empty speculation, make vegetarianism a household rule, and treat Chan meditation as statecraft.

sentences.zh: 一二人倡於前，千百人和於後。

translations.literal: One or two lead in front, hundreds and thousands harmonize behind.
translations.idiomatic: One or two take the lead, and hundreds and thousands follow.

sentences.zh: 甚有出則官服，入則僧衣。

translations.literal: Some even go out in official robes and enter in monk's robes.
translations.idiomatic: Some even wear official robes abroad and monastic robes at home.

sentences.zh: 惑智驚愚，駭人觀聽。

translations.literal: Bewildering the wise and startling the foolish, shocking people's eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: They bewilder the learned, alarm the simple, and shock all who see and hear them.

sentences.zh: 亮吉前在內廷，執事曾告之曰：『某等親王十人，施齋戒殺者已十居六七，羊豕鵝鴨皆不入門。』

translations.literal: Liangji formerly in the inner court, his colleagues once told him: 'Of us princes, ten men—those who keep vegetarian fasts and abstain from killing already number six or seven out of ten; sheep, pigs, geese, and ducks none enter our doors.'
translations.idiomatic: When I was in the inner court, a colleague told me: 'Of us ten princes, six or seven already keep vegetarian fasts and abstain from killing—sheep, pigs, geese, and ducks never enter our doors.'

sentences.zh: 及此回入都，而士大夫持齋戒殺又十居六七矣。

translations.literal: When returning to the capital this time, among scholar-officials those holding vegetarian fasts and abstaining from killing again number six or seven out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am back in the capital, six or seven out of ten literati keep vegetarian fasts and abstain from killing as well.

sentences.zh: 深恐西晉祖尚玄虛之習复見於今，則所關世道人心非小也。

translations.literal: Deeply fearing that the Western Jin custom of revering the abstruse and empty might reappear today—then what is involved in the spirit of the age and people's hearts is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: I deeply fear that the Western Jin fashion for empty speculation may reappear today; what is at stake in the spirit of the age and the hearts of the people is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 何以言賞罰仍不嚴明也？

translations.literal: Why say that rewards and punishments are still not strict and clear?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say that rewards and punishments are still not strict and clear?

sentences.zh: 自徵苗匪、教匪以來，福康安、和琳、孫士毅則蒙蔽欺妄於前，宜綿、惠齡、福寧則喪師失律於後，又益以景安、秦承恩之因循畏葸，而川、陝、楚、豫之民，遭劫者不知幾百萬矣。

translations.literal: Since the campaigns against Miao bandits and sect rebels, Fu Kang'an, He Lin, and Sun Shiyi deceived and concealed in the beginning; Yi Mian, Hui Ling, and Fu Ning lost armies and violated discipline afterward; further added Jing'an and Qin Cheng'en's procrastination and timidity—and the people of Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, and Henan who suffered plunder number surely several millions.
translations.idiomatic: Since the campaigns against the Miao and the sect rebels, Fu Kang'an, He Lin, and Sun Shiyi deceived and concealed at the outset; Yi Mian, Hui Ling, and Fu Ning lost armies and violated discipline later on; to these were added Jing'an and Qin Cheng'en's procrastination and timidity—and the people of Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, and Henan who suffered devastation must number several millions.

sentences.zh: 已死諸臣姑置勿論，其現在者未嘗不議罪也。

translations.literal: The ministers already dead may be set aside without discussion; those still living have not failed to be judged guilty.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers who are already dead may be set aside; those still living have not escaped censure.

sentences.zh: 然重者不過新疆換班，輕者不過大營轉餉；

translations.literal: Yet the severe punishment is no more than transfer to Xinjiang on rotation; the light is no more than supplying provisions at the great camp;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the heaviest penalty has been no more than rotation to Xinjiang; the lightest no more than supplying the main camp;

sentences.zh: 甚至拏解來京之秦承恩，則又給還家產，有意復用矣；

translations.literal: Even Qin Cheng'en, who was escorted as prisoner to the capital, then had family property returned, with intent to employ again;
translations.idiomatic: even Qin Cheng'en, who was brought to the capital under arrest, had his family property restored and is evidently to be employed again;

sentences.zh: 屢奉嚴旨之惠齡，則又起補侍郎。

translations.literal: Hui Ling, who repeatedly received stern edicts, then was raised again to fill the post of Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Ling, who had repeatedly received stern edicts, has been reappointed Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 夫蒙蔽欺妄之殺人，與喪師失律以及因循畏葸之殺人無異也，而猶邀寬典異數，亦從前所未有也。

translations.literal: Deceiving and concealing that kills people is no different from losing armies and violating discipline and procrastinating in timidity that kills people—yet they still receive lenient statutes and special treatment, also unprecedented.
translations.idiomatic: Deception and concealment that cost lives are no different from losing armies, violating discipline, or dithering in fear that cost lives—yet these men still receive lenient and extraordinary treatment, something never seen before.

sentences.zh: 故近日經略以下、領隊以上，類皆不以賊匪之多寡、地方之蹂躪掛懷。

translations.literal: Therefore recently from commissioners downward and column leaders upward, all generally do not care about the number of bandit rebels or the trampling of regions.
translations.idiomatic: Hence commissioners and column leaders alike generally pay no heed to how many rebels remain or how badly the countryside is ravaged.

sentences.zh: 彼其心未始不自計曰：『即使萬不可解，而新疆換班，大營轉餉，亦尚有成例可援，退步可守。』

translations.literal: In their hearts they never fail to calculate for themselves: 'Even if utterly irredeemable, Xinjiang rotation and great camp supply still have precedents to cite, retreats to hold.'
translations.idiomatic: In their hearts they tell themselves: 'Even if all else fails, rotation to Xinjiang and supply duty at the main camp still offer precedents to cite and a line of retreat to hold.'

sentences.zh: 國法之寬，及諸臣之不畏國法，未有如今日之甚者。

translations.literal: The leniency of national law and the ministers' fearlessness of national law have never been as severe as today.
translations.idiomatic: Never has the law been so lax, or ministers so unafraid of the law, as today.

sentences.zh: 純皇帝之用兵金川、緬甸，訥親僨事，則殺訥親；

translations.literal: When the Pure Emperor used troops in Jinchuan and Burma, when Neqin failed, he killed Neqin;
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor campaigned in Jinchuan and Burma, Neqin failed and was executed;

sentences.zh: 額爾登額僨事，則殺額爾登額；

translations.literal: when E'erdeng'e failed, he killed E'erdeng'e;
translations.idiomatic: E'erdeng'e failed and was executed;

sentences.zh: 將軍、提、鎮之類，伏失律之誅者，不知凡幾。

translations.literal: among generals, regional commanders, and garrison commanders, those who suffered execution for violating discipline—who knows how many.
translations.idiomatic: generals, provincial commanders, and garrison commanders who suffered death for breach of discipline were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 是以萬里之外，得一廷寄，皆震懼失色，則馭軍之道得也。

translations.literal: Therefore ten thousand li away, upon receiving one court dispatch, all trembled in fear and changed color—thus the way of controlling armies was attained.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand li away, a single dispatch from court made every commander tremble and turn pale—such was the right way to command armies.

sentences.zh: 今自乙卯以迄己未，首尾五年，僨事者屢矣。

translations.literal: Now from yimao to jiwei, first to last five years, failures have been frequent.
translations.idiomatic: From 1795 to 1799, a full five years, failures have been repeated.

sentences.zh: 提、鎮、副都統、偏裨之將，有一膺失律之誅者乎？

translations.literal: Among regional commanders, garrison commanders, deputy commandants, and subordinate officers, has there been one who suffered execution for violating discipline?
translations.idiomatic: Has a single provincial commander, garrison commander, deputy commandant, or field officer suffered death for breach of discipline?

sentences.zh: 而欲諸臣之不玩寇、不殃民得乎？

translations.literal: Yet can one expect the ministers not to trifle with bandits and not harm the people?
translations.idiomatic: How then can one expect officials not to trifle with the enemy and not bring disaster on the people?

sentences.zh: 夫以純皇帝之聖武，又豈見不及此？

translations.literal: With the Pure Emperor's sacred martial prowess, how could his vision not reach this?
translations.idiomatic: With the late emperor's sacred martial prowess, could his vision have failed to reach this far?

sentences.zh: 蓋以歸政在即，欲留待皇上蒞政之初，神武獨斷，一新天下之耳目耳。

translations.literal: Presumably because abdication of power was imminent, he wished to reserve it for when Your Majesty first took the reins, to decide alone with divine martial spirit and renew the eyes and ears of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Presumably because abdication was near, he wished to leave this for Your Majesty's first days in power—to decide with your own sacred resolve and renew the eyes and ears of the empire.

sentences.zh: 倘蕩平尚無期日，而國帑日見銷磨，萬一支絀偶形，司農告匱。

translations.literal: If pacification still has no date in sight, while the national treasury daily is worn down, should shortage suddenly appear, the Minister of Revenue would report empty coffers.
translations.idiomatic: If pacification still has no end in sight while the treasury is worn down day by day, a sudden shortfall may leave the Minister of Revenue reporting empty coffers.

sentences.zh: 言念及此，可為寒心，此尤宜急加之意者也。

translations.literal: To speak and think of this can make one chill at heart—this especially deserves urgent attention.
translations.idiomatic: To reflect on this is chilling; this above all deserves your urgent attention.

sentences.zh: 何以言言路似通而未通也？

translations.literal: Why say the avenue of speech seems open yet is not open?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say the avenue of remonstrance seems open yet is not truly open?

sentences.zh: 九卿臺諫之臣，類皆毛舉細故，不切政要。

translations.literal: The ministers of the Nine Chief Offices and the censorate and remonstrance bureaus mostly pick at minute matters, not touching on essentials of government.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Chief Offices and the censorate mostly nitpick trifles and never touch what matters in government.

sentences.zh: 否則發人之陰私，快己之恩怨。

translations.literal: Otherwise they expose others' private matters, gratify their own enmities and favors.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise they expose private scandals to settle personal scores.

sentences.zh: 十件之中，幸有一二可行者，發部議矣，而部臣與建言諸臣，又各存意見，無不議駁，並無不通駁，則又豈國家詢及芻蕘、詢及瞽史之初意乎？

translations.literal: Of ten items, fortunately one or two may be feasible and are sent to the ministry for deliberation—but ministry officials and the memorializing officials again each hold opinions, none without debate and rebuttal, and none without thorough rebuttal—then how is this the original intent of the state inquiring of the grass cutter and inquiring of the blind historian?
translations.idiomatic: Of ten proposals, perhaps one or two are feasible and are sent to the ministries for deliberation—yet ministry officials and the memorialists again take opposing sides, debate everything, and rebut everything. How is this the state's original intent in seeking counsel from the humblest and the lowliest?

sentences.zh: 然或因其所言瑣碎，或輕重失倫，或虛實不審，而一概留中，則又不可。

translations.literal: Yet if because what they say is trivial, or weight and lightness are out of order, or truth and falsehood are unexamined, and all are retained at court, that again is not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to retain every memorial at court because it is trivial, disproportionate, or unverified would also be wrong.

sentences.zh: 其法莫如隨閱隨發，面諭廷臣，或特頒諭旨，皆隨其事之可行不可行，明白曉示之。

translations.literal: The method is none better than to review and issue as one goes, instruct the court ministers in person, or specially promulgate an edict—all according to whether the matter is feasible or not, clearly informing them.
translations.idiomatic: The better course is to read and respond as each memorial arrives—to instruct the court in person or issue a special edict, plainly stating whether the proposal is feasible or not.

sentences.zh: 即或彈劾不避權貴，在諸臣一心為國，本不必避嫌怨。

translations.literal: Even if impeachment does not avoid the powerful, among the ministers with one heart for the state, there is originally no need to avoid suspicion and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Even when impeachment does not spare the powerful, ministers who serve the state with one heart need not fear personal resentment.

sentences.zh: 以近事論，錢灃、初彭齡皆常彈及大僚矣，未聞大僚敢與之為仇也。

translations.literal: Taking recent events, Qian Feng and Chu Pengling both often impeached great officials, yet one has not heard that great officials dared make enemies of them.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Qian Feng and Chu Pengling often impeached high officials, yet no senior minister dared treat them as enemies.

sentences.zh: 若其不知國體，不識政要，冒昧立言，或攻發人之陰私，則亦不妨使眾共知之，以著其非而懲其後。

translations.literal: If they do not know the national dignity, do not understand essentials of government, rashly speak, or attack and expose others' private matters, then it is also not improper to let the multitude know together, to show their error and warn those who follow.
translations.idiomatic: If a memorialist does not understand the dignity of the state or the essentials of policy, speaks rashly, or attacks private scandals, let the court know openly—expose the fault and warn those who follow.

sentences.zh: 蓋諸臣既敢挾私而不為國，更可無煩君上之回護矣。

translations.literal: Since the ministers already dare to harbor private motives and not serve the state, all the more there is no need for the sovereign to shield them.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers dare to serve private ends rather than the state, Your Majesty need not shield them at all.

sentences.zh: 何以言吏治欲肅而未肅也？

translations.literal: Why say that official administration wishes to be rectified yet is not rectified?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say that official administration is meant to be rectified yet has not been rectified?

sentences.zh: 未欲吏治之肅，則督、撫、籓、臬其標準矣。

translations.literal: If one wishes official administration to be rectified, then governors-general, governors, provincial administration commissioners, and provincial judicial commissioners are the standard.
translations.idiomatic: If official administration is to be rectified, governors-general, governors, and provincial commissioners are the standard.

sentences.zh: 十馀年來，督、撫、籓、臬之貪欺害政，比比皆是。

translations.literal: For more than ten years, governors-general, governors, and provincial commissioners' greed, deceit, and harm to government have been everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years, greedy and corrupt governors and provincial commissioners have been everywhere.

sentences.zh: 幸而皇上親政以來，李奉翰已自斃，鄭元鸘已被糾，富綱已遭憂，江蘭已內改。

translations.literal: Fortunately since Your Majesty's personal rule, Li Fenghan has already died by himself, Zheng Yuanhong has already been impeached, Fu Gang has already suffered bereavement, Jiang Lan has already been transferred within.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately since Your Majesty took personal rule, Li Fenghan has died, Zheng Yuanhong has been impeached, Fu Gang has left office in mourning, and Jiang Lan has been transferred inland.

sentences.zh: 此外，官大省、據方面者如故也，出巡則有站規、有門包，常時則有節禮、生日禮，按年則又有幫費。

translations.literal: Besides these, great-province officials holding regional power remain as before: on inspection tours there are station fees and gate packets; in ordinary times there are festival gifts and birthday gifts; by the year there are also support fees.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond them, the great provincial officers remain as before: on tour they collect station fees and gate packets; in ordinary times festival gifts and birthday gifts; each year support fees as well.

sentences.zh: 升遷調補之私相餽謝者，尚未在此數也。

translations.literal: Private mutual gifts at promotion, transfer, and filling of posts are not yet counted in this number.
translations.idiomatic: The private gifts exchanged at promotions and transfers are not even included in this tally.

sentences.zh: 以上諸項，無不取之於州縣，州縣則無不取之於民。

translations.literal: All the above items are without exception taken from prefectures and counties; prefectures and counties without exception take from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Every item above is drawn from the prefectures and counties, and they in turn draw it all from the people.

sentences.zh: 錢糧漕米，前數年尚不過加倍，近則加倍不止。

translations.literal: Land tax and transport grain, in earlier years still no more than doubled; recently they are more than doubled without stop.
translations.idiomatic: Land tax and transport grain, which a few years ago were merely doubled, are now more than doubled.

sentences.zh: 督、撫、籓、臬以及所屬之道、府，無不明知故縱，否則門包、站規、節禮、生日禮、幫費無所出也。

translations.literal: Governors-general, governors, and provincial commissioners and their subordinate circuit and prefectural intendants—all without exception clearly know and deliberately indulge, otherwise gate packets, station fees, festival gifts, birthday gifts, and support fees would have nowhere to come from.
translations.idiomatic: Governors, provincial commissioners, and their circuit and prefectural subordinates all knowingly condone this—otherwise their gate packets, station fees, festival gifts, birthday gifts, and support fees would have no source.

sentences.zh: 州縣明言於人曰：『我之所以加倍加數倍者，實層層衙門用度，日甚一日，年甚一年。』

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties plainly tell people: 'The reason I double and multiply several times is truly that yamen expenses layer upon layer grow day by day and year by year.'
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county magistrates tell the people plainly: 'The reason I double and redouble levies is that expenses at every level of government grow worse day by day and year by year.'

sentences.zh: 究之州縣，亦恃督、撫、籓、臬、道、府之威勢以取於民，上司得其半，州縣之入己者亦半。

translations.literal: Investigating prefectures and counties, they also rely on the power and prestige of governors-general, governors, provincial commissioners, circuits, and prefectures to take from the people; superiors get half, what prefectures and counties keep for themselves is also half.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the magistrates too rely on the power of governors and commissioners to squeeze the people: half goes to their superiors, half they keep.

sentences.zh: 初行尚有畏忌，至一年二年，則成為舊例，牢不可破矣。

translations.literal: At first there was still fear and restraint; by one or two years it became an old precedent, firmly unbreakable.
translations.idiomatic: At first they still had some scruples; within a year or two it became fixed custom, impossible to break.

sentences.zh: 訴之督、撫、籓、臬、道、府，皆不問也。

translations.literal: Appeals to governors-general, governors, provincial commissioners, circuits, and prefectures—all go unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: Appeals to governors, commissioners, circuits, and prefectures go unanswered.

sentences.zh: 千萬人中，或有不甘冤抑，赴京控告者，不過發督撫審究而已，派欽差就訊而已。

translations.literal: Among tens of millions, perhaps some who will not endure wrongful oppression go to the capital to lodge complaints—nothing more than sending the governor-general and governor to investigate, or dispatching an imperial commissioner to inquire on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Of millions of people, a few who cannot bear injustice may go to the capital to complain—but the outcome is only an order for the provincial authorities to investigate, or an imperial commissioner sent to inquire.

sentences.zh: 試思百姓告官之案，千百中有一二得直者乎？

translations.literal: Consider: in cases of common people suing officials, of a thousand or hundred is there one or two who obtain justice?
translations.idiomatic: Consider: of a thousand cases in which commoners sue officials, do one or two obtain justice?

sentences.zh: 即欽差上司稍有良心者，不過設為調停之法，使兩無所大損而已。

translations.literal: Even imperial commissioners and superiors with slight conscience do no more than set up methods of mediation, so that both sides suffer no great loss.
translations.idiomatic: Even an imperial commissioner or superior with some conscience merely arranges a compromise so that neither side suffers too greatly.

sentences.zh: 若欽差一出，則又必派及通省，派及百姓，必使之滿載而歸而心始安，而可以無後患。

translations.literal: If an imperial commissioner goes out, then again he must assess the whole province and assess the common people, must make them return fully loaded before his heart is at ease and he can be without later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Once an imperial commissioner is dispatched, he assesses the whole province and the common people alike, and will not rest until he returns with his pockets full and no fear of later trouble.

sentences.zh: 是以州縣亦熟知百姓之技倆不過如此，百姓亦習知上控必不能自直，是以往往至於激變。

translations.literal: Therefore prefectures and counties also well know that the common people's tricks go no further than this; the common people also habitually know that appealing upward certainly cannot obtain justice for themselves—therefore they often come to violent upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates know the people's remedies go no further than this; the people know appeals to the capital never bring justice—so matters often end in violent upheaval.

sentences.zh: 湖北之當陽，四川之達州，其明效大驗也。

translations.literal: Dangyang in Hubei and Dazhou in Sichuan are clear proof on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: Dangyang in Hubei and Dazhou in Sichuan are glaring proof.

sentences.zh: 亮吉以為今日皇上當法憲皇帝之嚴明，使吏治肅而民樂生；

translations.literal: Liangji considers that today Your Majesty should follow the Manifest Emperor's strict clarity, cause official administration to be rectified and the people to rejoice in life;
translations.idiomatic: Liangji believes that today Your Majesty should follow the strict clarity of the Manifest Emperor, rectify official administration, and let the people live in peace;

sentences.zh: 然後法仁皇帝之寬仁，以轉移風俗，則文武一張一弛之道也。」

translations.literal: then follow the Benevolent Emperor's generous benevolence, to transform customs—then this is the civil and martial way of one tension and one relaxation."
translations.idiomatic: then follow the generous benevolence of the Benevolent Emperor to transform customs—such is the civil and martial way of tension and release."

translations.literal: Thus closed the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the memorial.

sentences.zh: 書達成親王​​，以上聞，上怒其語戇，落職下廷臣會鞫，面諭勿加刑，亮吉感泣引罪，擬大辟，免死遣戍伊犁。

translations.literal: The memorial reached the Prince of Cheng, was reported above; the emperor was angry at his blunt words, stripped office and handed down to ministers for joint inquiry, personally instructed not to add torture; Liangji wept moved and pleaded guilty; sentenced to death by decapitation, death remitted, exiled to garrison at Yili.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the Prince of Cheng and was reported to the throne. The emperor was angered by its blunt tone, stripped Hong of office, and referred him to a joint inquiry by the court. He personally instructed that no torture be applied. Hong wept, accepted guilt, and was sentenced to decapitation; the death penalty was remitted and he was exiled to Yili.

sentences.zh: 明年，京師旱，上禱雨未應，命清獄囚，釋久戍。

translations.literal: The next year, the capital was drought; the emperor prayed for rain without response, ordered clearing of prison inmates, released long exiles.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the capital suffered drought. The emperor prayed for rain without result and ordered prisons cleared and long-term exiles released.

sentences.zh: 未及期，詔曰：「罪亮吉後，言事者日少。

translations.literal: Before the term arrived, an edict said: 'After punishing Liangji, those who speak on affairs daily grow fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Before the term expired, an edict said: 'Since Liangji was punished, memorialists have grown fewer day by day.

sentences.zh: 即有，亦論官吏常事，於君德民隱休戚相關之實，絕無言者。

translations.literal: Even when there are some, they also discuss routine matters of officials; on realities intimately connected with sovereign virtue and the people's hidden suffering, there is absolutely no one who speaks.
translations.idiomatic: When they do speak, it is only on routine official business; no one addresses what truly touches Your Majesty's virtue and the people's hidden suffering.

sentences.zh: 豈非因亮吉獲罪，鉗口不复敢言？

translations.literal: Is it not because Liangji received punishment, mouths were clamped and they no longer dare speak?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not because Liangji's punishment has silenced them and they no longer dare speak?

sentences.zh: 朕不聞過，下情复壅，為害甚鉅。

translations.literal: I do not hear of faults, lower sentiments again are blocked— the harm is very great.
translations.idiomatic: I hear no report of my faults, and the people's grievances are again blocked—a very great harm.

sentences.zh: 亮吉所論，實足啟沃朕心，故銘諸座右，時常觀覽，勤政遠佞，警省朕躬。

translations.literal: What Liangji discussed truly suffices to enrich and moisten my heart; therefore I inscribe it at my seat's side, constantly view it, diligently govern and keep the sycophantic far, warn and examine my person.
translations.idiomatic: What Liangji wrote truly enlightens my mind. I have inscribed it beside my seat and read it often—to govern diligently, keep flatterers at a distance, and examine myself.

sentences.zh: 今特宣示亮吉原書，使內外諸臣，知朕非拒諫飾非之主，實為可與言之君。

translations.literal: Now I specially proclaim Liangji's original writing, to make inner and outer ministers know that I am not a lord who rejects remonstrance and covers faults, but truly a ruler with whom one may speak.
translations.idiomatic: I now publish Liangji's original text so that all officials within and without may know I am not a ruler who rejects counsel and covers faults, but one to whom they may speak frankly.

sentences.zh: 諸臣遇可與言之君而不與言，負朕求治苦心。」

translations.literal: If the ministers encounter a ruler with whom they may speak yet do not speak, they betray my bitter heart in seeking good government.'
translations.idiomatic: If officials meet a ruler willing to hear them yet remain silent, they betray my earnest desire for good government.'

sentences.zh: 即傳諭伊犁將軍，釋亮吉回籍。

translations.literal: Immediately transmit instruction to the Yili general, release Liangji to return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered the Yili general to release Liangji and send him home.

sentences.zh: 詔下而雨，御製詩紀事，注謂：「本日親書諭旨，夜子時甘霖大沛。

translations.literal: When the edict descended, rain fell; the emperor composed a poem to record the event, noting: 'This day I personally wrote the edict; at the midnight hour sweet rain poured greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell as soon as the edict was issued. The emperor composed a poem on the event, noting: 'I wrote the edict myself today; at midnight a great sweet rain poured down.

sentences.zh: 天鑑捷於呼吸，益可感畏。」

translations.literal: Heaven's mirror is swifter than breath— all the more to be felt in awe.'
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's response was swifter than a breath—how much more to be revered in awe.'

sentences.zh: 亮吉至戍甫百日而赦還，自號更生居士。

translations.literal: Liangji had reached exile only a hundred days when pardoned and returned; he styled himself Layman Born Again.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had been at his post of exile only a hundred days when he was pardoned and returned; he styled himself Layman Born Again.

sentences.zh: 後十年，卒於家。

translations.literal: Ten years later, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later he died at home.

sentences.zh: 所著書多行世。

translations.literal: His written works mostly circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his writings remain in circulation.

sentences.zh: 管世銘，字緘若，與亮吉同里。

translations.literal: Guan Shiming, style name Jianruo, was of the same native place as Liangji.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Shiming, style name Jianruo, was a fellow townsman of Hong Liangji.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十三年進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1778 and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director, and served as Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to director and served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 深通律令，凡讞牘多世銘主奏。

translations.literal: He was deeply versed in statutes and ordinances; of judicial documents most were drafted under Shiming's lead.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply versed in law; most judicial memorials were drafted under his direction.

sentences.zh: 屢從大臣赴浙江、湖北、吉林、山東按事，大學士阿桂尤善之，倚如左右手。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed great ministers to Zhejiang, Hubei, Jilin, and Shandong to investigate affairs; Grand Secretary A Gui especially favored him and relied on him as on right and left hands.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly accompanied senior ministers on investigations in Zhejiang, Hubei, Jilin, and Shandong. Grand Secretary A Gui favored him especially and relied on him as on his own hands.

sentences.zh: 時和珅用事，世銘憂憤，與同官論前代輔臣賢否，語譏切無所避。

translations.literal: At the time Heshen held power; Shiming was anxious and indignant, and with fellow officials discussed whether former-age chief ministers were worthy or not, his words sarcastic and cutting without avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Heshen held power. Guan was troubled and angry; with colleagues he discussed whether chief ministers of past dynasties had been worthy, speaking with biting sarcasm and holding nothing back.

sentences.zh: 會遷御史，則大喜，夜起傍徨，草疏將劾之，詔仍留軍機處。

translations.literal: When he was about to be transferred to censor, he was greatly delighted, rose at night pacing in circles, drafted a memorial about to impeach him—but an edict still retained him at the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: When he was due for promotion to censor he was overjoyed, rose at night in agitation, and drafted a memorial to impeach Heshen—but an edict kept him at the Grand Council instead.

sentences.zh: 故事，御史留直者，儀注仍視郎官，不得專達封事。

translations.literal: By precedent, a censor retained on duty still followed ceremonial rules as a director, and could not exclusively present sealed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, a censor who remained on Grand Council duty was still treated ceremonially as a director and could not submit sealed memorials on his own.

sentences.zh: 世銘自言愧負此官，阿桂慰之曰：「報稱有日，何必急以言自見。」

translations.literal: Shiming himself said he was ashamed to fail this office; A Gui comforted him, saying: 'A day to repay the appointment will come—why must you hurry to make yourself seen through words.'
translations.idiomatic: Guan said he had failed the office. A Gui comforted him: 'Your day to repay the appointment will come—why must you hurry to make yourself known through words.'

sentences.zh: 蓋留直阿桂所請，隱全之，使有待。

translations.literal: This was because retention on duty was requested by A Gui, who secretly protected him completely, letting him wait.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui had requested that he remain on duty, secretly protecting him and bidding him wait.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1798.

sentences.zh: 谷際岐，字西阿，雲南趙州人。

translations.literal: Gu Jiqi, style name Xi'a, was a native of Zhaozhou in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Jiqi, style name Xi'a, was a native of Zhaozhou, Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，與校四庫全書。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and participated in collating the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1775, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and helped collate the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries.

sentences.zh: 充會試同考官，所拔多知名士。

translations.literal: Served as associate examiner for the metropolitan examination; those he selected were mostly famous scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He served as associate examiner for the metropolitan examination and selected many men who later won renown.

sentences.zh: 乞養歸，主講五華書院，教士有法。

translations.literal: Begged leave to nurse parents and returned; lectured at Wuhua Academy; teaching scholars had method.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to care for his parents and went home to head the Wuhua Academy, where he taught with real discipline.

sentences.zh: 連丁父母憂，服闋，起原官。

translations.literal: In succession observed parents' mourning; when mourning ended, resumed original office.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned both parents in succession; when the mourning period ended, he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，遷御史。

translations.literal: Jiaqing year 3, transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1798 he was transferred to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 時教匪擾數省，師久無功，際岐遍訪人士來京者，具得其狀。

translations.literal: At the time sectarian rebels disturbed several provinces; armies long without success; Jiqi everywhere visited people coming to the capital and fully learned the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Sectarian rebels were ravaging several provinces and the campaigns dragged on without victory. Jiqi questioned every traveler who came to Beijing until he had the full picture.

sentences.zh: 四年春，上疏，略曰：「竊見三年以來，先帝頒師征討邪教，川、陝責之總督宜綿，巡撫惠齡、秦承恩；

translations.literal: Year 4 spring, submitted memorial, summary saying: "I have seen that for three years the late emperor has dispatched armies to campaign against heterodox teachings; Sichuan and Shaanxi charged to Governor-General Yi Mian, Grand Coordinators Hui Ling and Qin Cheng'en;
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1799 he submitted a memorial that began: "For three years now the late emperor has sent armies against the sectarians. Sichuan and Shaanxi fall to Governor-General Yi Mian and Grand Coordinators Hui Ling and Qin Cheng'en;

sentences.zh: 楚北責之總督畢沅、巡撫汪新。

translations.literal: North Chu charged to Governor-General Bi Yuan, Grand Coordinator Wang Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei and northern Huguang to Governor-General Bi Yuan and Grand Coordinator Wang Xin.

sentences.zh: 諸臣釀釁於先，藏身於後，止以重兵自衛，裨弁奮勇者，無調度接應，由是​​兵無鬥志。

translations.literal: These officials brewed trouble in front and hid in the rear, only using heavy troops to defend themselves; assistant commanders who fought bravely had no coordination or relief, and thereby the troops lost fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: These ministers provoked the trouble up front and hid in the rear, guarding only themselves with heavy forces. Brave subordinate officers received no coordination or relief—and so the men lost heart for battle.

sentences.zh: 川、楚傳言云：'賊來不見官兵面，賊去官兵才出現。

translations.literal: Sichuan and Chu rumor says: 'When bandits come one does not see government troops' faces; when bandits go, government troops only then appear.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan and Hubei had a saying: "When the rebels come you never see a government soldier's face; when the rebels leave, the troops finally show up."

sentences.zh: '又云：'賊去兵無影，兵來賊沒踪。

translations.literal: 'Again it says: 'When bandits go the troops have no shadow; when troops come the bandits leave no trace.
translations.idiomatic: Another line ran: "The rebels are gone and the troops vanish; the troops arrive and the rebels disappear."

sentences.zh: 可憐兵與賊，何日得相逢？

translations.literal: Pity the troops and the bandits—on what day can they meet?
translations.idiomatic: Poor soldiers and poor rebels—when will they ever meet?

sentences.zh: '前年總督勒保至川，大張告示，痛責前任之失，是其明證。

translations.literal: The year before, Governor-General Le Bao arrived in Sichuan, posted broad notices, and bitterly blamed his predecessors' failures—that is clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, when Governor-General Le Bao reached Sichuan, he put up broad proclamations bitterly condemning his predecessors' failures—that itself was proof enough.

sentences.zh: 畢沅、汪新相繼殂逝，景安繼為總督。

translations.literal: Bi Yuan and Wang Xin died in succession; Jing An succeeded as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan and Wang Xin died in succession, and Jing An succeeded as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 今宜綿、惠齡、秦承恩縱慢於左，景安怯玩於右，勒保縱能實力剿捕，陝、楚賊多，起滅無時，則勒保終將掣肘。

translations.literal: Now Yi Mian, Hui Ling, and Qin Cheng'en are indulgent and slow on the left; Jing An is timid and indifferent on the right. Even if Le Bao can with real strength suppress and capture, Shaanxi and Chu have many bandits rising and perishing without cease, and Le Bao will in the end be checked and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Mian, Hui Ling, and Qin Cheng'en are slack and negligent on one flank; Jing An is timid and indifferent on the other. Even if Le Bao fights in earnest, rebels in Shaanxi and Hubei rise and fall without end, and Le Bao will in the end be hamstrung.

sentences.zh: 欽惟先帝昔徵緬甸，見楊應琚挑撥掩覆之罪，立予拿問。

translations.literal: Respectfully consider: the late emperor formerly campaigned in Burma, saw Yang Yingju's crime of provocation and concealment, and immediately had him seized for inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how the late emperor, campaigning in Burma, found Yang Yingju guilty of provocation and concealment and had him seized at once for trial.

sentences.zh: 今宜綿等曠玩三年之久，幸荷寬典，而轉益懷安，任賊越入河南盧氏、魯山等縣。

translations.literal: Now Yi Mian and the rest have been negligent for three years, fortunately received lenient treatment, yet instead grew more complacent and let bandits cross into Lushi, Lushan, and other counties in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Mian and the rest have been negligent for three full years, spared by imperial leniency only to grow more complacent, and allowed rebels to push into Lushi, Lushan, and other counties in Henan.

sentences.zh: 景安雖無吞餉聲名，而罔昧自甘，近亦有賊焚掠襄、光各境，均為法所不容。

translations.literal: Jing An, though without a reputation for embezzling rations, is willfully ignorant and self-content; recently bandits have also burned and looted through Xiangyang and Guanghua—all of which the law cannot permit.
translations.idiomatic: Jing An may not have a reputation for swallowing army funds, but he is willfully obtuse; of late rebels have burned and pillaged through Xiangyang and Guanghua—and all of this the law cannot abide.

sentences.zh: 況今軍營副封私札，商同軍機大臣改壓軍報。

translations.literal: Moreover, sealed private letters now come from military camps, and officials consult with Grand Council ministers to alter and suppress battle reports.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, sealed private letters are now coming from military camps, and officials are conspiring with Grand Council ministers to tamper with and suppress battle reports.

sentences.zh: 供據已破，雖由內臣聲勢，而彼等掩覆僨事，情更顯然。

translations.literal: The evidence is already exposed; although inner eunuchs lent their influence, these men's concealment and bungling are even plainer.
translations.idiomatic: The evidence is already exposed. Even if inner eunuchs lent their influence, these men's concealment and bungling are plainer still.

sentences.zh: 請旨懲究，另選能臣，與勒保會同各清本境，則軍令風行，賊必授首。

translations.literal: I beg an imperial decree to punish and investigate, separately select capable ministers, and send them with Le Bao to pacify each province in its own territory; then military orders will run like the wind and the bandits will surely present their heads.
