translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to punish and investigate, choose other able men, and send them with Le Bao to pacify each province in its own territory. Then army orders will run like the wind, and the rebels will surely lose their heads.

sentences.zh: 比年發餉至數千萬，軍中子女玉帛奇寶錯陳，而兵食反致有虧。

translations.literal: In recent years pay issued has reached tens of millions; in the camps women, children, jade, silk, and rare treasures are piled in profusion, yet the soldiers' rations themselves fall short.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years pay has run to tens of millions, while camps teem with women, jade, silk, and curios—yet the soldiers' rations themselves fall short.

sentences.zh: 載贓而歸，風盈道路，嘲之者有'與其請餉，不如書會票'之語。

translations.literal: They return laden with loot and the roads buzz with gossip; mockers say, 'Rather than beg for pay, better to write a draft at the money-shop.'
translations.idiomatic: Men return laden with plunder and the roads buzz with gossip. Mockers say it is easier to draw up a draft at the money-shop than to beg the army for pay.

sentences.zh: 先帝嚴究軍需局，察出四川漢州知州與德楞泰互爭報銷，及湖北道員胡齊崙侵餉數十萬，一則追賠，一則拿究。

translations.literal: The late emperor strictly investigated the military supplies bureau, found the Hanzhou prefect in Sichuan disputing expense reports with Degengtai, and the Hubei circuit intendant Hu Qilun embezzling hundreds of thousands in pay—one ordered to repay, the other seized for trial.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor cracked down on the military supplies bureau, found the Hanzhou prefect in Sichuan disputing accounts with Degengtai, and Hubei circuit intendant Hu Qilun embezzling hundreds of thousands in pay—one ordered to repay, the other seized for trial.

sentences.zh: 他屬類此者必多，尤宜急易新手清釐。

translations.literal: Other jurisdictions surely have many similar cases; it is especially urgent to put new hands in charge and audit the books.
translations.idiomatic: Many other districts surely have like cases, and new men ought to be put in charge at once to audit the books.

sentences.zh: 則侵盜之跡，必能破露，不但兵餉與善後事宜均得充裕，銷算亦不敢牽混矣。」

translations.literal: Then traces of embezzlement can surely be exposed; not only will army pay and postwar relief be ample, but no one will dare doctor the accounts."
translations.idiomatic: Embezzlement will then come to light; army funds and postwar relief will both be ample, and no one will dare doctor the accounts."

translations.literal: End of the memorial quotation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he closed the memorial.

sentences.zh: 間又上疏曰：「教匪滋擾，始於湖北宜都聶傑人，實自武昌府同知常丹葵苛虐逼迫而起。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he again submitted a memorial saying: "Sectarian rebels spreading disturbance began with Nie Jieren of Yidu in Hubei, but in truth arose because Wuchang subprefect Chang Dankui drove the people with cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted another memorial: "The sectarian turmoil began with Nie Jieren of Yidu in Hubei—yet it truly arose because Wuchang subprefect Chang Dankui drove the people with cruelty.

sentences.zh: 當教匪齊麟等正法於襄陽，匪徒各皆斂戢。

translations.literal: When sectarian rebels Qi Lin and others were lawfully executed at Xiangyang, the outlaws all restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When sectarian leaders such as Qi Lin were lawfully executed at Xiangyang, the outlaws all quieted down.

sentences.zh: 常丹葵素以虐民喜事為能，乾隆六十年，委查宜都縣境，哧詐富家無算，赤貧者按名取結，納錢釋放。

translations.literal: Chang Dankui was known for abusing the people and manufacturing cases; in Qianlong year 60 he was delegated to investigate Yidu county, intimidated and extorted countless wealthy families, and for the utterly poor took bonds by name and released them for money.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Dankui had long made a name for tormenting the people and manufacturing cases. In 1795 he was sent to investigate Yidu county, intimidated and shook down countless wealthy families, and even extorted the destitute by name, releasing them only after they paid.

sentences.zh: 少​​得供據，立與慘刑，至以鐵釘釘人壁上，或鐵鎚排擊多人。

translations.literal: With the slightest evidence he immediately inflicted cruel torture, even nailing people to walls with iron spikes or lining up many men for blows with iron hammers.
translations.idiomatic: On the slightest evidence he tortured at once—nailing men to walls with iron spikes or lining up crowds to be beaten with iron hammers.

sentences.zh: 情介疑似，則解省城，每船載一二百人，飢寒就斃，浮屍於江。

translations.literal: When the case was merely suspicious, he sent them to the provincial capital; each boat carried one or two hundred men, who died of hunger and cold, their corpses floating on the river.
translations.idiomatic: When a case was even slightly doubtful, he shipped prisoners to the provincial capital—two hundred to a boat—until hunger and cold killed them and corpses floated down the river.

sentences.zh: 歿獄中者，亦無棺殮。

translations.literal: Those who died in prison also received no coffin or burial.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died in prison were not even given coffins.

sentences.zh: 聶傑人號首富，屢索不厭，村黨結連拒捕。

translations.literal: Nie Jieren was called the richest man in the district; Chang extorted him again and again without satisfaction, and the village clans banded together to resist arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Jieren was the district's wealthiest man; Chang squeezed him without end until the villages banded together to resist arrest.

sentences.zh: 宜昌鎮總兵突入遇害，由是宜都、枝江兩縣同變。

translations.literal: The Yichang garrison commander rushed in and was killed; thereby Yidu and Zhijiang both counties rose together.
translations.idiomatic: The Yichang brigade commander stormed in and was killed, and Yidu and Zhijiang counties rose together.

sentences.zh: 襄陽之齊王氏、姚之富，長陽之覃加耀、張正謨等，聞風並起，遂延及河南、陝西。

translations.literal: At Xiangyang, Lady Qi Wang and Yao Zhifu; at Changyang, Tan Jiayao, Zhang Zhengmo, and others—hearing the news all rose together, and the trouble spread to Henan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Qi of Wang, Yao Zhifu at Xiangyang, Tan Jiayao and Zhang Zhengmo at Changyang, and others took up arms on the news, and the revolt spread into Henan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 此臣所聞官逼民反之最先最甚者也。

translations.literal: This is what I have heard of officials driving the people to rebel—the earliest and gravest case.
translations.idiomatic: This is the earliest and gravest case I know of officials driving the people to rebel.

sentences.zh: 臣思教匪之在今日，自應盡黨梟磔。

translations.literal: I consider that the sectarian rebels of today should of course have their whole party dismembered and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Today the sectarian rebels must of course be exterminated to the last.

sentences.zh: 而其始猶是百數十年安居樂業人民，何求何憾，甘心棄身家、捐​​性命，鋌而走險耶？

translations.literal: Yet at the start they were still people who had lived in peace and work for a hundred or several tens of years—what did they seek, what did they regret, that they willingly abandoned family and person, gave up life, and ran to desperate risk?
translations.idiomatic: Yet at first they were people who had lived in peace for generations—what did they lack, what grievance drove them to abandon home and life and take desperate risks?

sentences.zh: 臣聞賊當流竄時，猶哭念皇帝天恩，殊無一言怨及朝廷。

translations.literal: I hear that when the rebels were driven to flight they still wept and spoke of the emperor's heavenly grace, and had not a single word of complaint against the court.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that even in flight the rebels wept over the emperor's grace and never spoke a word of blame against the throne.

sentences.zh: 向使地方官仰體皇仁，察教於平日，撫弭於臨時，何至如此？

translations.literal: If only local officials had looked up to embody imperial benevolence, watched sects in ordinary times, and soothed and settled them when trouble came—how could it have come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Had local officials embodied the throne's benevolence, watched sects in peacetime, and soothed trouble when it arose, how could matters have come to this?

sentences.zh: 臣為此奏，固為官吏指事聲罪，亦欲使萬禩子孫知我朝無叛民，而後見恩德入人，天道人心，協應長久，昭昭不爽也。

translations.literal: I submit this memorial both to name and accuse the officials involved, and also to let ten thousand generations of descendants know that our dynasty has no rebellious people, and thereafter see that grace enters men's hearts, that heaven's way and men's hearts together respond for long endurance, clear and without error.
translations.idiomatic: I submit this memorial to name the guilty officials, but also so that ten thousand generations may know our dynasty has no rebellious people—that imperial grace reaches men's hearts, and that heaven and human will together sustain the realm, clear and sure.

sentences.zh: 常丹葵逞虐一時，上廑聖仁，下殃良善，罪豈容誅？

translations.literal: Chang Dankui for a time indulged in cruelty, above troubling imperial benevolence, below harming the good—can his crime be spared execution?
translations.idiomatic: Chang Dankui tyrannized for a season, affronting the throne's benevolence and harming the innocent—how can his crime go unpunished?

sentences.zh: 應請飭經略勒保嚴察奏辦。

translations.literal: He should be ordered through Grand Coordinator Le Bao to investigate strictly and report for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Grand Coordinator Le Bao be ordered to investigate strictly and report for punishment.

sentences.zh: 又現奉恩旨，凡受撫來歸者，令勒保傳喚同知劉清，同川省素有清名之州縣，妥議安插。

translations.literal: Moreover, an imperial grace decree now commands that all who accept pacification and return be ordered through Le Bao to summon Subprefect Liu Qing, together with Sichuan prefects and magistrates of long-standing clean reputation, to deliberate proper resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial decree now orders Le Bao to summon Subprefect Liu Qing and Sichuan officials of long-standing clean reputation to settle all who accept pacification and return.

sentences.zh: 楚地曾經滋擾者，亦應安集。

translations.literal: Places in Chu that were once disturbed should also be settled and gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Regions in Huguang that were once disturbed should be settled as well.

sentences.zh: 臣聞被擾州縣，逃散各戶之田廬婦女，多歸官吏壓賣分肥。

translations.literal: I hear that in disturbed prefectures and counties, the fields, houses, and women of households that fled and scattered mostly fell to officials who forced sales and divided the profit.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that in ravaged districts the fields, homes, and women of fleeing households were mostly seized by officials, sold under pressure, and the profits divided among them.

sentences.zh: 是始不顧其反，終不原其歸。

translations.literal: Thus at first they did not care that the people rebelled, and in the end they did not forgive their return.
translations.idiomatic: At first they did not care that the people rebelled; in the end they would not forgive their return.

sentences.zh: 不知民何負於官，而效尤靦忍至於此極？

translations.literal: I do not know what the people owed officials that they imitated such shameless cruelty to this extreme.
translations.idiomatic: What had the people done to officials that they copied such shameless cruelty to the utmost?

sentences.zh: 若得懲一儆眾，自可群知洗濯。

translations.literal: If one can be punished to warn the multitude, the rest will naturally know to cleanse themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Punish one to warn the rest, and the whole body of officials will know to reform.

sentences.zh: 宣奉德意，所關於國家苞桑之計匪細也。」

translations.literal: To proclaim and uphold the imperial virtue concerns the state's plan of rooted mulberry—not a small matter."
translations.idiomatic: To proclaim and uphold imperial grace touches the nation's very roots—it is no small matter."

sentences.zh: 兩疏上，仁宗並嘉納施行。

translations.literal: Both memorials were submitted; the Jiaqing Emperor praised and adopted them all for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Both memorials were submitted, and the Jiaqing Emperor praised and put them into effect.

sentences.zh: 尋遷給事中，稽察南新倉，巡視中城。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to supervising secretary, inspected the Nanxin granary, and patrolled the central city.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made supervising secretary, assigned to inspect the Nanxin granary and patrol the central city.

sentences.zh: 雲南鹽法，官運官銷，日久因緣為奸，按口比銷，民不堪命；

translations.literal: Yunnan's salt law used government transport and government sale; over time opportunities bred corruption, sales were apportioned by head count, and the people could not bear the burden;
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's salt monopoly used official transport and official sale; over time it bred corruption, sales were apportioned per capita, and the people could not endure it;

sentences.zh: 又威遠調取民夫，按名折銀，折後又徵實夫，迤西道屬數十州縣，同時閧變，解散後不以實聞，官吏骫法如故。

translations.literal: Moreover, Weiyuan conscripted laborers, commuted names to silver payments, and after commutation again levied actual laborers; dozens of prefectures and counties under the Yixi circuit rose in riot together, and after dispersal the truth was not reported—officials bent the law as before.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyuan also conscripted laborers, commuted names to cash, then levied real labor again; dozens of counties under the Yixi circuit rioted together, and after the crowds dispersed officials reported falsely and bent the law as before.

sentences.zh: 際岐上疏痛陳其害，下雲南督撫察治。

translations.literal: Jiqi submitted a memorial bitterly stating the harm, and the case was sent down to Yunnan's governor-general and grand coordinator for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqi memorialized bitterly on the harm, and the throne ordered Yunnan's governor-general and grand coordinator to investigate.

sentences.zh: 總督富綱請改鹽法以便民，巡撫江蘭方內召，欲沮其事，際岐复疏爭。

translations.literal: Governor-General Fu Gang requested to change the salt law to benefit the people; Grand Coordinator Jiang Lan had just been summoned to the capital and wished to obstruct the matter; Jiqi again memorialized in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Fu Gang asked to reform the salt law for the people's sake; Grand Coordinator Jiang Lan, newly summoned to court, tried to block it, and Jiqi memorialized again in protest.

sentences.zh: 初彭齡繼為巡撫，際岐門下士也，熟聞其事，始疏請鹽由灶煎灶賣，民運民銷，一祛積弊，民大便。

translations.literal: Chu Pengling succeeded as grand coordinator; he was Jiqi's student, knew the affair well, and at last memorialized that salt should be boiled and sold at the furnaces, transported and sold by the people, removing accumulated abuses at a stroke—the people were greatly relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pengling, Jiqi's student, succeeded as grand coordinator, knew the affair well, and at last memorialized that salt be boiled and sold at the furnaces and carried and sold by the people, sweeping away old abuses—the people were greatly relieved.

sentences.zh: 語詳鹽法志。

translations.literal: The account is given in detail in the Monograph on Salt Administration.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the Monograph on Salt Administration.

sentences.zh: 蔡永清者，總督陳輝祖家奴，擁厚貲居京師，以助賑敘五品職銜，出入輿馬，揖讓公卿間。

translations.literal: Cai Yongqing was a household slave of Governor-General Chen Huizu; he possessed great wealth and lived in the capital, received a fifth-rank title for aiding famine relief, went in and out by carriage, and bowed and yielded among dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yongqing was a household slave of Governor-General Chen Huizu who amassed great wealth in the capital, bought a fifth-rank title by aiding famine relief, rode in carriages, and mingled bowing with grandees and ministers.

sentences.zh: 際岐疏劾，自大學士慶桂、硃珪以下，多所指斥，下刑部鞫訊，褫永清職銜，際岐坐論奏未盡實，降授刑部主事。

translations.literal: Jiqi memorialized in impeachment; from Grand Secretary Qing Gui and Zhu Gui downward many were named and rebuked; the case went to the Ministry of Punishments for inquiry; Yongqing's title was stripped; Jiqi was faulted for memorializing without full truth and demoted to a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqi impeached him, naming many from Grand Secretaries Qing Gui and Zhu Gui downward; the Ministry of Punishments tried the case, stripped Yongqing's title, and demoted Jiqi to a clerk in that ministry for memorializing without full substantiation.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in due course to director.

sentences.zh: 以老乞休，貧不能歸，主講揚州孝廉堂垂十年，卒。

translations.literal: On grounds of age he begged retirement; too poor to return home, he lectured at Yangzhou's Xiaoliang Hall for nearly ten years, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on grounds of age, too poor to go home, and lectured at Yangzhou's Xiaoliang Hall for nearly ten years until he died.

sentences.zh: 自乾隆末，雲南之官於朝以直言著者，尹壯圖、錢灃，時以際岐並稱焉。

translations.literal: From the late Qianlong reign, Yunnan officials at court famed for blunt speech were Yin Zhuangtu and Qian Feng; at the time Jiqi was ranked with them.
translations.idiomatic: From the late Qianlong era, Yunnan men at court famed for blunt speech were Yin Zhuangtu and Qian Feng; Jiqi was ranked with them.

sentences.zh: 李仲昭，字次卿，廣東嘉應人。

translations.literal: Li Zhongzhao, style name Ciqing, was a native of Jiaying in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongzhao, style name Ciqing, was a native of Jiaying, Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷御史。

translations.literal: Jiaqing year 7 jinshi, selected Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1802, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and transferred to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 長蘆鹽商偽造加重法馬，每引浮百斤，損課滯銷。

translations.literal: Changlu salt merchants forged heavier standard weights; each salt quota floated a hundred jin extra, harming revenue and slowing sales.
translations.idiomatic: Changlu salt merchants forged heavier standard weights, padding each quota by a hundred jin, cutting revenue and slowing sales.

sentences.zh: 商人查有圻家​​鉅富，交通朝貴。

translations.literal: The merchant Zha Youqi's family was immensely wealthy and cultivated ties with court nobles.
translations.idiomatic: The merchant Zha Youqi's family was immensely wealthy and cultivated ties with court nobles.

sentences.zh: 自給事中花傑劾蘆鹽加價，連及大學士戴衢亨，不得直，且被譴，遂無敢言者。

translations.literal: Since Supervising Secretary Hua Jie impeached the Changlu salt price increase, implicating Grand Secretary Dai Yuheng, he did not obtain justice and was moreover rebuked—after that no one dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: After Supervising Secretary Hua Jie impeached the Changlu salt price hike and implicated Grand Secretary Dai Yuheng, he failed to obtain justice and was rebuked, and thereafter no one dared speak.

sentences.zh: 仲昭疏劾之，戶部猶袒商，或騰蜚語，謂仲昭索賄不遂。

translations.literal: Zhongzhao memorialized in impeachment; the Board of Revenue still shielded the merchants, and some spread rumors that Zhongzhao had sought bribes without success.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhao impeached them, but the Board of Revenue still shielded the merchants, and some spread rumors that he had sought bribes in vain.

sentences.zh: 仁宗方幸熱河，命留京王大臣同鞫，得舞弊狀，有圻論如律，在事降革有差，人咸側目。

translations.literal: The Jiaqing Emperor was at Rehe; he ordered princes and ministers remaining in the capital to try the case jointly; fraud was established; Youqi was sentenced according to law; those involved were demoted or dismissed in varying degrees; all looked on in awe.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaqing Emperor was at Rehe and ordered princes and ministers in the capital to try the case jointly. Fraud was proved; Youqi was sentenced by law; those involved were demoted or dismissed in varying degrees, and all looked on in awe.

sentences.zh: 仲昭又劾吏部京察不公，亦鞫實。

translations.literal: Zhongzhao again impeached the Board of Civil Office for unfair capital evaluation; that too was tried and found true.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhao again impeached the Board of Civil Office for unfair capital evaluation, and that too was proved true.

sentences.zh: 既而赴戶部點卯，杖責書吏，戶部摭其事奏劾，下吏部議。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went to the Board of Revenue for roll call, beat and punished clerks, and the board seized on the affair to memorialize in impeachment; the case went down to the Board of Civil Office for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he went to the Board of Revenue for roll call and beat the clerks; the board seized on the affair to impeach him, and the case went to the Board of Civil Office for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 群欲以傾仲昭，侍郎初彭齡號剛正，以妻喪在告，語人曰：「諸人欲報怨，加以莫須有之罪。

translations.literal: The crowd wished to overturn Zhongzhao; Vice Minister Chu Pengling, known as upright, was on leave for his wife's mourning and said to others: "These men wish to settle scores and add a crime that does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Many wished to ruin Zhongzhao; Vice Minister Chu Pengling, known for integrity, was on leave for his wife's mourning and told others: "These men wish to settle scores and invent a crime out of nothing.

sentences.zh: 李御史有言膽，台中何可無此人？」

translations.literal: Censor Li has the courage to speak—how can the censorate be without such a man?"
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li has the courage to speak—how can the censorate do without such a man?"

sentences.zh: 部員聞彭齡言，遽議降四級，甫兩日而奏上，仲昭竟黜。

translations.literal: Board members heard Pengling's words, hurriedly deliberated a demotion of four ranks, and within only two days the memorial went up—Zhongzhao was dismissed after all.
translations.idiomatic: Board members heard Pengling's words, hurriedly voted a four-rank demotion, and within two days the memorial went up—Zhongzhao was dismissed after all.

sentences.zh: 石承藻，字黼庭，湖南湘潭人。

translations.literal: Shi Chengzao, style name Futing, was a native of Xiangtan in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chengzao, style name Futing, was a native of Xiangtan, Hunan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年一甲三名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: Jiaqing year 13, third place in the first class of the jinshi examination, appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1808 he took third place in the first class of the jinshi examination and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷御史、給事中，敢言有聲。

translations.literal: Transferred to censor and supervising secretary; his bold speech won renown.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the censorate and made supervising secretary, winning renown for bold speech.

sentences.zh: 王樹勳者，江都人，乾隆末入京應試不售，乃於廣慧寺為僧，名曰明心。

translations.literal: Wang Shuxun was a native of Jiangdu; at the end of the Qianlong reign he came to the capital to sit for examinations without success, then became a monk at Guanghui Temple with the religious name Mingxin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuxun was from Jiangdu; at the end of the Qianlong reign he came to the capital to sit for examinations without success, then became a monk at Guanghui Temple under the name Mingxin.

sentences.zh: 開堂說法，假扶乩卜筮，探刺士大夫陰私，揚言於外，人益崇信。

translations.literal: He opened a hall to preach the dharma, feigned spirit-writing and divination, probed and pierced the private affairs of scholar-officials, and proclaimed them abroad—people revered him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a preaching hall, feigned spirit-writing and divination, pried into officials' private affairs, and spread the secrets abroad—so people revered him all the more.

sentences.zh: 達官顯宦，每有皈依受戒為弟子者。

translations.literal: High officials and eminent ministers often took refuge, received precepts, and became his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: High officials and eminent ministers often took refuge, received precepts, and became his disciples.

sentences.zh: 硃珪正人負重望，亦與交接。

translations.literal: Zhu Gui was an upright man of heavy reputation and also associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gui, an upright man of great standing, also associated with him.

sentences.zh: 時和珅為步軍統領，訪捕治罪，以賄得末減，勒令還俗，遂遊蕩江湖。

translations.literal: At the time Heshen was metropolitan infantry commander; he sought, arrested, and punished him; through bribery he received the lightest sentence, was ordered to return to lay life, and then wandered the rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen, then metropolitan infantry commander, hunted him down; he bribed his way to a lighter sentence, was forced back to lay life, and wandered the country.

sentences.zh: 值川、楚匪亂，投效松筠軍中，以談禪投所好，使易裝入賊寨說降，獎予七品官銜，洊擢襄陽知府。

translations.literal: When Sichuan and Chu bandit turmoil arose, he entered Songyun's army, pleased him by preaching Chan, was sent in disguise into rebel camps to persuade surrender, was rewarded with a seventh-rank title, and was promoted in succession to prefect of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out in Sichuan and Hubei, he joined Songyun's army, won favor by preaching Chan, was sent in disguise into rebel camps to negotiate surrender, was given a seventh-rank title, and rose in succession to prefect of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 數年，入覲京師，不改故態。

translations.literal: After several years he came to the capital for audience and did not change his old ways.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he came to the capital for audience and did not change his old ways.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書金光悌延醫子病，怵以禍福，光悌長跪請命，為時所嗤。

translations.literal: Minister of Punishments Jin Guangti invited him to treat his son's illness; he intimidated him with fortune and misfortune; Guangti knelt long to beg for his command, and the age mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Punishments Jin Guangti invited him to treat his son's illness; he threatened him with fortune and disaster; Guangti knelt long to beg his counsel, and the age mocked him.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十年，承藻疏請澄清流品，劾樹勳，下刑部鞫實，褫職，枷號兩月，發黑龍江充當苦差。

translations.literal: Jiaqing year 20, Chengzao memorialized requesting clarification of official ranks, impeached Shuxun; the case went to the Ministry of Punishments, was tried and found true; his office was stripped; he was cangued for two months and sent to Heilongjiang to serve hard labor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1815 Chengzao memorialized to clarify official ranks and impeached Shuxun; the Ministry of Punishments tried the case, stripped his office, cangued him for two months, and sent him to Heilongjiang for hard labor.

sentences.zh: 仁宗獎承藻曰：「真御史也！」

translations.literal: The Jiaqing Emperor praised Chengzao, saying: "A true censor!"
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaqing Emperor praised Chengzao: "A true censor!"

sentences.zh: 詔斥被惑諸臣，有玷官箴。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked the deluded ministers, saying they had stained the official rule.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked the deluded ministers for staining the official rule.

sentences.zh: 其已故者免議，侍郎蔣予蒲、宋鎔以下，黜降有差。

translations.literal: Those already deceased were exempted from deliberation; Vice Ministers Jiang Yupu, Song Rong, and below were dismissed or demoted in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Those already dead were spared further inquiry; Vice Ministers Jiang Yupu, Song Rong, and others below them were dismissed or demoted in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，湘潭有土、客械鬥之獄，侍郎週系英與巡撫吳邦慶互劾。

translations.literal: Year 24, Xiangtan had a case of armed fighting between native and guest communities; Vice Minister Zhou Xiying and Grand Coordinator Wu Bangqing impeached each other.
translations.idiomatic: In 1819 Xiangtan saw armed fighting between native and migrant communities; Vice Minister Zhou Xiying and Grand Coordinator Wu Bangqing impeached each other.

sentences.zh: 承藻適在籍，系英子汝楨致書承藻詢其事，為邦慶所發，承藻牽連降秩。

translations.literal: Chengzao happened to be in his native place; Xiying's son Ruzhen wrote Chengzao to inquire about the affair; Bangqing exposed it, and Chengzao was implicated and demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzao happened to be home on leave; Xiying's son Ruzhen wrote to ask him about the affair; Bangqing exposed the letter, and Chengzao was implicated and demoted.

sentences.zh: 久之不復遷，終光祿寺署正。

translations.literal: For a long time he was not promoted again and ended as acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was not promoted again for a long time and ended his career as acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 論曰：仁宗詔求直​​言，下至末吏平民，皆得封章上達，言路大開。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: The Jiaqing Emperor issued an edict seeking blunt speech; down to the lowest clerks and common people, all could seal memorials and have them reach the throne—the path of remonstrance was greatly opened.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: The Jiaqing Emperor called for blunt speech; from the lowest clerks to common people, all could submit sealed memorials to the throne, and the path of remonstrance stood wide open.

sentences.zh: 科道中竭誠獻納，如衛謀論福康安貪婪，不宜配享太廟。

translations.literal: Among the censorate and supervising secretaries many offered counsel with full sincerity, as when Wei Mou argued that Fukang'an was greedy and unfit to share sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and supervising secretaries offered counsel with full sincerity, as when Wei Mou argued that Fukang'an was greedy and unfit to share sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 馬履泰論景安畏縮偷安，老師糜餉，及教匪宜除，難民宜撫；

translations.literal: Ma Lvtai argued that Jing An was timid, shrank back, and sought ease, that old armies wasted rations, that sectarian rebels should be eliminated, and that refugees should be comforted;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lvtai argued that Jing An was timid and indifferent, that armies wasted rations in stalemate, that sectarian rebels must be eliminated, and that refugees must be comforted;

sentences.zh: 又論百齡舉劾失當。

translations.literal: He also argued that Bai Ling's recommendations and impeachments were improper.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Bai Ling's recommendations and impeachments were improper.

sentences.zh: 張鵬展論金光悌專擅刑部，戀司職不去。

translations.literal: Zhang Pengzhan argued that Jin Guangti monopolized the Ministry of Punishments and clung to his office without leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pengzhan argued that Jin Guangti monopolized the Ministry of Punishments and clung to his post.

sentences.zh: 週栻論疆臣參劾屬員，不舉劣跡，恐悃愊無華者以失歡被劾；

translations.literal: Zhou Shi argued that frontier ministers impeaching subordinates did not cite bad conduct, fearing that honest and unadorned men might be impeached for losing favor;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shi argued that frontier governors impeaching subordinates cited no misdeeds, lest honest and unadorned men be punished merely for falling from favor;

sentences.zh: 又論硃珪以肩輿擅入禁門，無無君之心，而有無君之跡。

translations.literal: He also argued that Zhu Gui, by entering the forbidden gate in a shoulder-carriage without permission, had no heart disloyal to the ruler but did have the appearance of disloyalty to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Zhu Gui, entering the forbidden gate by sedan chair without leave, had no disloyal intent but left the appearance of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 沈琨論宜興庇護屬員，致興株系諸生大獄；

translations.literal: Shen Kun argued that in Yixing, sheltering subordinates led to a great case in which many students were implicated and punished;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Kun argued that sheltering subordinates in Yixing had led to a great case in which many students were swept up and punished;

sentences.zh: 又諫阻東巡。

translations.literal: He also remonstrated to block the eastern tour.
translations.idiomatic: He also remonstrated against the eastern tour.

sentences.zh: 蕭芝論端正風俗，宜崇醇樸。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhi argued that to rectify customs one ought to honor simplicity and plainness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhi argued that to rectify public morals the court should honor plain and unadorned ways.

sentences.zh: 王寧煒論用人宜習其素，不可因保舉遽加升用；

translations.literal: Wang Ningwei argued that in employing men one ought to know their long-standing character and must not promote them hastily on the strength of recommendation alone;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ningwei argued that appointments should rest on long knowledge of a man's character, not hasty promotion on recommendation alone;

sentences.zh: 又論督撫壅蔽之習，及士民捐輸之累，州縣折收之患。

translations.literal: He also discussed the habit of governors and governors-general in concealing reports, the burden of gentry and commoners' voluntary contributions, and the harm of prefectures and counties' surcharges in collection.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke of governors' habit of concealing reports, the burden of gentry donations, and the harm of prefectural surcharge collection.

sentences.zh: 遊光繹論大臣未盡和衷，武備未盡整飭，原效魏元成十思疏以裨治化。

translations.literal: You Guangyi argued that great ministers had not yet achieved full harmony, that military preparations had not yet been fully rectified, and that he wished to emulate Wei Zhengyuan's Ten Reflections memorial to aid good government.
translations.idiomatic: You Guangyi argued that ministers still lacked harmony, military readiness was still incomplete, and offered to follow the model of Wei Zheng's Ten Reflections to aid governance.

sentences.zh: 諸人所言，雖有用有不用，當時皆推讜直。

translations.literal: What these men said, though some was adopted and some was not, at the time all were praised as candid and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Not every word was acted on, but at the time all were praised as candid and upright.

sentences.zh: 又龔鏜當鬆筠因諫東巡獲罪，密疏复陳，自庀身後事而後上，卒蒙寬宥。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Gong Fu saw Songyun punished for remonstrating against the eastern tour, he submitted a secret memorial stating his views again, put his affairs in order for after his death, and only then presented it—ultimately receiving lenient pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong Fu saw Songyun punished for opposing the eastern tour, he drafted a secret memorial, settled his affairs, and only then submitted it—and in the end was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 其章疏多不傳，稽之史牒，旁見紀載，謇諤盈廷，稱盛事焉。

translations.literal: Most of their memorials have not been transmitted; searching historical records, one sees them mentioned in passing—frank remonstrance filled the court, and it was called a grand occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Most of their memorials do not survive, yet historical records mention them in passing—frank speech filled the court, and the age was called a great one for remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 洪亮吉諸人身雖遭黜，言多見採，可以無憾。

translations.literal: Although Hong Liangji and the others personally suffered dismissal, their words were largely adopted, and they may be without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Liangji and the others were punished, yet much of what they said was heeded—they had little to regret.

sentences.zh: 或猶以時方清明，目亮吉之效痛哭流涕者為多事，過矣。

translations.literal: Some still, because the times seemed clear and bright, regarded Liangji's manner of weeping and shedding tears as making too much of things—this was excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Some, thinking the times already clear, called Liangji's tearful remonstrance excessive—but they were wrong.
